Many of the clubs are calling for a far more severe punishment for City given the commission’s conclusion that without the hugely inflated income they would have breached Premier League and Uefa spending limits in multiple seasons, and will also lobby to ensure that the whole process is concluded before the end of the season.

“Relegation to the Championship for one season would be insufficient,” a club source told the Guardian. “The commission has to arrive at a punishment that is proportionate for years of sustained and deliberate cheating, as well as providing a strong deterrent to it happening again.”

The Premier League is in a difficult position, as it is also eager to prevent further mass litigation against City by rivals seeking financial recompense. Burnley were awarded £35m at an arbitration hearing earlier this year after suing Everton on the back of their PSR breach, which they claimed led to their relegation at the end of the 2021-22 season, a decision that has set a precedent for clubs claiming compensation following regulatory offences.

Manchester United, Arsenal, Tottenham and Liverpool all reserved their rights to sue City in the event of a guilty verdict two years ago, and have already held informal conversations about whether to pursue a claim now the judgment has been published. While those clubs will all arrive at individual decisions, the extent of City’s punishment could prove critical to their thinking.

Many of the top-flight clubs remain unhappy with the Premier League’s decision to reach an agreed sanction this year with Chelsea of a £10m fine after they self-reported the previous owners making unlawful payments to players and agents during the Roman Abramovich era.

Sports.title: ‘I am here more than ever’: Guardiola backs Manchester City owners over guilty verdicts
Sports.content:
Pep Guardiola has thrown his support behind Manchester City after the club were found guilty of all charges of breaching Premier League financial rules over a nine-year period, telling fans: “We will get through this together.”

Guardiola left City in the summer after a trophy-laden decade in charge, with his first two seasons falling within the period investigated by the independent commission. The Spaniard remains a close ally of the chief executive, Ferran Soriano, who brought him to England, the pair having previously worked together at Barcelona. City maintain their innocence and are set to appeal against the decision before Friday’s deadline.

“I want every single Manchester City fan across the world to know I am here; more than ever,” Guardiola posted on social media. “I am, always have been, always will, be behind my club, my owner, my chairman, Ferran, the players, staff, Enzo [Maresca] and you, our unique supporters. Let me be clear: we will get through this together. I love you all.”

Twenty trophies were won in the 10 years Guardiola managed City and he was frequently asked about the charges that hung over the club for much of his tenure. The 55-year-old has consistently reiterated his faith in what he was told by the club’s Abu Dhabi ownership while the investigation was ongoing, with charges first brought against the club in February 2023. “I trust them,” Guardiola said in May. “I spoke with them and trust how they behave and how they did.”

Upon Guardiola’s departure, it was confirmed that he would continue as a global ambassador for City Football Group, which involves him giving “technical advice to the clubs in the group, working on specific projects and collaborations”.

Meanwhile the former City chair David Bernstein has described the situation at the club as “beyond awful” and called for the board to stand down. “I can’t think of a penalty strong enough for this, really. I mean, this is absolutely terrible,” said Bernstein, who was chair between 1998 and 2003.

“I want to raise another question, and that is the position of the board of directors. Because the directors ‌of the club, including the chief executive, who’s been there for years and went ‌through this period, are responsible for the running of the club in every respect.

“If this was a public company of some sort, the directors would have to stand down or be suspended pending the outcome of all this, appeal or no appeal. I don’t ‌think the present management can credibly continue.”

Andrée Jeglertz, the Manchester City Women’s head coach, insisted that it had been a case of “business as usual” for his team as they prepare to host Real Madrid in the Women’s Champions League on Thursday. Asked if he echoed Guardiola’s position and if he would back the club in spite of the Premier League’s guilty verdict, Jeglertz said: “Definitely. I’m working [at] this club now, and that’s definitely what I’m hired for, for sure.”

The Swede declined to comment further when asked if he had been given any assurances that the women’s team would not be affected by the matter.

Jeglertz insisted his side, who won the Women’s Super League title last season, were focused only on football, saying: “We haven’t changed anything, we just keep on doing everything we normally do.”

Sports.title: Hampton’s heroics preserve WCL point for Chelsea on Bompastor’s OL Lyonnes return
Sports.content:
There were plenty of encouraging signs for Chelsea as they claimed a valuable point in the Champions League on their head coach Sonia Bompastor’s return to face her former team OL Lyonnes.

The goalless draw was a slow-burner but concluded with a flurry of late action where both teams missed chances to steal the points. However a draw felt fair on a night when Chelsea’s double pivot of Keira Walsh and Lexi Potter in midfield continued to flourish, three days after they similarly impressed in Sunday’s victory over Arsenal.

OL Lyonnes had scored eight times in their first fixture in the league phase, away against the Swiss side Servette, but Chelsea looked comfortable for large periods and Bompastor said: “I’m really proud of my team, being able to not concede here. We are happy also with the ball, the way we performed, we were able to exploit different spaces. The only thing that was missing was the goal.”

The French side had scored at least seven times in all four matches they had played in all competitions this season. Given that formidable form and the confidence in the hosts’ front line, Chelsea were grateful to Hannah Hampton for her sharp save from Salma Paralluelo on 20 minutes, and similarly glad to see Melchie Dumornay’s powerful effort fizz just wide of a post a few minutes later.

Chelsea had the majority of the ball, however. Potter, buoyed by the receipt of her first senior England call-up on Tuesday, gave as good as she got in the physical battle in midfield and generally appeared at home on this stage, at the record eight-time European champions, which will have been pleasing for Sarina Wiegman. The 20-year-old, alongside her compatriot Walsh, helped Chelsea maintain an element of control.

Unlike Chelsea, who played a fiery derby against Arsenal in England, the top French sides were able to rest at the weekend, in between the first two European fixtures, as the French league helps its sides stay fresh for the Champions League. Other French top-tier sides played in the League Cup instead. It was therefore reasonable to assume that Lyonnes might look the stronger as this contest went on. That was true to a degree, as Chelsea – missing Katie McCabe through illness – tired slightly late on.

Quick Guide WCL roundup: Barcelona win big again Show Barcelona continued their emphatic start to their title defence by brushing aside Roma 6-0 in the Italian capital. Caroline Graham Hansen got Barça off the mark in Rome inside 20 minutes. A Shukurat Oladipo own goal put them two up before the break and Clàudia Pina (pictured) made the points safe just after, before Graham Hansen and Pina both got their second goals and Ewa Pajor put the cherry on the cake late on. Bayern Munich, who gave up a two-goal lead last week to draw with Manchester City, were in danger of behind held again at Benfica, but won 3-0 thanks to three goals from in the last 16 minutes from Klara Bühl, Pernille Harder and Franziska Kett. Juventus downed Häcken 3-0 in Sweden to make up for last Tuesday’s defeat by Benfica. The Spanish World Cup winner Alba Redondo scored again, making it three goals in as many games and seven in 12 in all competitions since joining from Real Madrid. AFP Photograph: Domenico Cippitelli/Shutterstock Editorial Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

It was Chelsea, however, who started the second period the brighter. They thought they deserved a penalty when Tarciane took out Sjoeke Nüsken at the far post, just as the Chelsea midfielder looked certain to score, but after a check on the monitor, the referee concluded that Lucy Bronze had been interfering with play from an offside position as the ball was crossed. Tarciane was booked for her challenge, nonetheless.

Bompastor, who won this competition as a player and a manager with Lyonnes, brought on Lauren James to give her side a different forward dynamic with just over half an hour remaining, while Lyonnes introduced a former Ballon d’Or winner in Ada Hegerberg, but neither side looked likely to break the deadlock until much later, as the off-the-ball qualities of both teams appeared to cancel each other out. A cautious approach, from Chelsea in particular, was understandable; this was, by a significant distance, the toughest-looking fixture of their league-phase matches, against last season’s runners-up.

View image in fullscreen Chelsea’s Lexi Potter impressed on the big stage after her first England call-up. Photograph: Alexandre Dimou/Reuters

Lyonnes, owned by the London City Lionesses and Washington Spirit owner, Michele Kang, have high ambitions to win this title this term. They thought they had scored on 72 minutes, when Paralluelo struck a low shot into the bottom corner, but the offside flag was raised.

Just a few minutes later, a moment of real controversy arose, as Chelsea were awarded a penalty for a foul by Damaris Egurrola on James. After a video review, the decision was overturned with the referee appearing to conclude that James had made contact with Egurrola rather than the other way around. The Lyonnes midfielder, though, looked very fortunate to escape, having mistimed her tackle and also missed the ball completely. Chelsea were exasperated. Bompastor said later that she felt it was a “clear penalty”.

James had Chelsea’s best chance late on but her close-range strike was blocked by Mala Grohs in goal, before Hampton saved superbly from Hegerberg at the other end, as the match finally came to life in the very late stages and Maika Hamano dragged a shot wide deep into stoppage time. But Chelsea will be satisfied with this point.

Sports.title: ‘I like him as a No 9’: Bellingham a striking alternative for England, says Tuchel
Sports.content:
Thomas Tuchel’s hunt for alternatives to Harry Kane has led to him identifying Jude Bellingham as an option at No 9 for England. Kane continued his remarkable scoring record in the 2-0 win against Czechia in the Nations League on Tuesday, moving to 87 goals in 123 international appearances with a late strike in Prague, but he has little cover up front.

There is no prospect yet of Tuchel having to consider life without Kane. The England head coach backed the 33-year-old striker to last another decade at the highest level, tipped him to reach a century of international goals soon, and said England cannot expect to produce a replica of their greatest forward. However, there is concern over whether England have enough depth in attack.

Ollie Watkins and Ivan Toney have been overlooked for this camp. Dominic Calvert-Lewin, who came on for Kane during the defeat by Spain on Saturday, is 29 and has four goals in 13 caps. Liam Delap, the 23-year-old Nottingham Forest forward, is yet to earn a senior call-up and it was noted that Bellingham led the line after coming on for Kane in the closing stages against Czechia.

“You will not get another Harry Kane, first of all,” Tuchel said. “We look for different solutions. We finished the game with Jude as a No 9. There will be someone else but it will not be Harry or a copy of Harry. We will find a solution when it comes to it but maybe not me. It might be another 10 years.”

Bellingham wore the captain’s armband after coming off the bench in Prague on Tuesday. “I like him as a [No] 9,” Tuchel said. “Then he can contribute to both sides and overloads the sides and doesn’t affect so much of the balance. We found a bit of a new role for him in the last match, as a central [No] 10, so he can go to both sides and it is more of a 4-2-3-1 than a 4-3-3 to have Harry and Jude closer together and to give them a chance to overload both sides.

“We are working on that. Jude in general should always be able to go through the last line and be able to end up in the box. He is a natural goalscorer and has the hunger to be on the scoreboard. He wants to have the decisive action so it makes not a huge difference if he plays as a [No] 9 or a [No] 10.”

England moved second in Nations League Group A3 after seeing off Czechia, who were reduced to 10 men midway through the first half. Anthony Gordon opened the scoring and Kane finished well late on.

“The ball falls down and you see Harry taking the shot and that is exactly the player you want it to drop down to,” Tuchel said. “He does it in every single match. The highest level of finishing.”

Tuchel was the manager who took Kane to Bayern Munich in 2023. Uli Hoeness, Bayern’s honorary president, has since said the former Tottenham striker is the club’s greatest signing. “That is so beautiful as it tells me everyone can see his true value and his personality,” Tuchel said. “It is not easy to change and to come to Bayern Munich when you win, win, win and it is a big club. You are under the spotlight and he won everyone over.”

England’s next assignment is a trip to Rijeka to face Croatia on Saturday. It remains to be seen if Tuchel sticks with Trent Alexander-Arnold after the right-back marked his first international appearance since June 2025 by creating Gordon’s goal.

“Trent’s outstanding,” Kane said. “The delivery, the passing range, the crossing but also today defensively he was outstanding. He’s a fantastic player. Trent just has to keep his head down, keep working hard. He’s been great in camp so far. He’s showing to the boss that he wants to be here.”

Sports.title: Leah Williamson blunder gifts Paris FC a point as Arsenal’s struggles continue
Sports.content:
Renée Slegers did not attend the post‑match press conference, the manager understood to have been too furious after Arsenal threw away a two-goal lead in their draw with Paris FC on Wednesday night.

The assistant coach Aaron D’Antino stepped in to speak to the media instead of Slegers, after a disastrous mix-up between the goalkeeper Misa Rodríguez and the centre-back Leah Williamson gifted Paris FC a penalty that Maeline Mendy converted to deny Arsenal all three points in the Champions League.

“The most frustrating part is how much we are working behind the scenes to try and turn this around, and it is just not going our way at the moment,” D’Antino said.

Alessia Russo and Georgia Stanway had given the Gunners a two-goal lead but Clara Mateo pulled one back before Williamson handled the ball after the referee deemed play to have restarted from a goal-kick when Rodríguez passed it to her.

D’Antino said: “If we’re looking at what we can control, it’s just passing the ball to Leah. From what I remember seeing, the ball was still rolling and she was moving it to Leah for her to take the goal-kicks as we normally do. So maybe the learning in that is how we get the ball to Leah, so we don’t put ourselves in that situation. But as far as we’re concerned, that’s not a penalty … we haven’t taken a goal-kick, there’s no advantage gained by Leah stopping the ball.”

It has been a tough start to the season for Arsenal, who are up against it in the title race with only five points from their opening four games, and the closing stages of the match in Paris delivered another gut punch.

Quick Guide WCL roundup: Barcelona win big again Show Barcelona continued their emphatic start to their title defence by brushing aside Roma 6-0 in the Italian capital. Caroline Graham Hansen got Barça off the mark in Rome inside 20 minutes. A Shukurat Oladipo own goal put them two up before the break and Clàudia Pina (pictured) made the points safe just after, before Graham Hansen and Pina both got their second goals and Ewa Pajor put the cherry on the cake late on. Bayern Munich, who gave up a two-goal lead last week to draw with Manchester City, were in danger of behind held again at Benfica, but won 3-0 thanks to three goals from in the last 16 minutes from Klara Bühl, Pernille Harder and Franziska Kett. Juventus downed Häcken 3-0 in Sweden to make up for last Tuesday’s defeat by Benfica. The Spanish World Cup winner Alba Redondo scored again, making it three goals in as many games and seven in 12 in all competitions since joining from Real Madrid. AFP Photograph: Domenico Cippitelli/Shutterstock Editorial Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

Paris FC had promised another tricky test, with teams that are happy to concede possession frustrating an Arsenal side that just cannot seem to find their way through low blocks. Chelsea had read that script on Sunday: they were organised at the back and punished Arsenal’s profligacy and failure to make their early dominance count.

At the Stade Jean-Bouin, which sits in the shadow of Paris Saint-Germain’s Parc des Princes, the story was familiar. As a result, it was less a wave of relief that swept through the pocket of travelling Arsenal fans and the players when their first goal went in and more a tsunami. It had looked as if Arsenal’s hesitancy had cost them a possible opening again when Stanway prodded the ball towards Russo but the England forward took several touches to create the space to shoot before firing her low effort in.

With the home team forced to come out more, that it took only five minutes after the restart for Arsenal to double their lead was no surprise. It was a stylish finish from Stanway that gave Arsenal breathing space, the midfielder pushed Emily Fox’s cross forward a little with her chest before lashing a volley in from close range.

View image in fullscreen Georgia Stanway is embraced after scoring Arsenal’s second goal before their evening took a turn for the worse. Photograph: Catherine Steenkeste/Reuters

However, only 22 minutes of comfort followed, before the team that inflicted a shock win on penalties to knock Arsenal out of qualifying in 2023 pulled the goal back that would test the Gunners’ resolve.

It was a mix-up between the centre-backs Lotte Wubben-Moy and Williamson that delivered the goal. The pair both moved to close down Evelyne Viens and the Canadian forward slipped the ball wide to Clara Mateo who raced free, rounded Rodríguez and slotted into the empty net.

It was tense as the clock ticked down. Paris posed a threat throughout, but the leveller followed the most calamitous of mistakes by Arsenal. Rodríguez collected the ball for a goal-kick, rolled it on to the pitch and then passed it to Williamson who bent and stopped the ball with her hand. The referee’s whistle went and she pointed to the spot, with Rodríguez deemed to have taken the goal-kick while Williamson clearly assumed she was being given the ball to take it. VAR did not intervene and Mendy converted from the spot, driving powerfully into the bottom corner.

It was a bruising end to another bruising game for Arsenal, who really need some luck to go their way to lift the increasing pressure. Meanwhile, Slegers’s decision to avoid talking after the game will have only ramped that pressure up further ahead of a must-win game against league leaders Manchester City on Sunday.

Sports.title: Craig Bellamy urges Wales improvement but wary of Norway’s threat
Sports.content:
Craig Bellamy has said Wales must improve against Norway on Thursday after appearing unrecognisable in their defeat against Denmark, and highlighted their next opponents’ run to the World Cup quarter-finals as proof of their talent.

Wales host Norway in Cardiff hoping to record their first win since last November and their first since promotion to Nations League A. “This team has been on a surge,” he said of Ståle Solbakken’s side. “They are progressing and they will keep going as well – they ain’t going away, especially with the youngsters they’ve got coming through. We’ve all been waiting [for them to flourish]. But it was coming and it’s come with a bang.”

Bellamy said Norway having two teams in the Champions League – Bodø/Glimt and Viking – would have been a “miracle a number of years ago”. Addressing the Norwegian media at his pre-match press conference on Wednesday, Bellamy said: “I think you’re all sneakily hoping we don’t talk about you as much but the World Cup exposes you. But I’m on to yous. I know what you’re up to and I know your younger age groups are getting even stronger.

“Sander [Berge], [Martin] Ødegaard and [Erling] Haaland, they are really close friends and their three sons are all the same age, born within a few months of each other. They’re already preparing the next generation, so we’re all in trouble.”

Addressing Wales’s 2-0 defeat in Copenhagen on Sunday, Bellamy said: “I didn’t recognise anything about us in the game and that was hard. We didn’t look clear in what we were doing, we were ‘in between’ and that comes from myself. I want us to improve as a team and I want to improve.”

Meanwhile, the Brentford defender Kristoffer Ajer insisted Haaland has displayed the same personality as normal amid the noise surrounding Manchester City after the club were found guilty of breaching the Premier League’s financial rules across a nine-year period. “Ever since I met him he’s been a guy that brings a lot of energy and joy to the group and that’s the biggest compliment I always give Erling,” Ajer said.

“When people ask about him, he hasn’t changed one bit since the first time I met him, even though he’s the biggest star on the planet right now. He’s been exactly the same the last few days as well, which is not a surprise for me.”

Solbakken, Norway’s head coach for the past six years, said “everything’s fine” with Haaland, who has scored three goals in his past two matches, and played down the idea that the City verdict has been a distraction. “[He’s been] very good, scoring goals,” Solbakken said.

“He missed one chance against Portugal that he usually doesn’t miss and that’s the only thing I can say negative, because he’s on fire.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Bellamy said he did not expect Haaland to be bothered by his club’s situation at Cardiff City Stadium. The Wales head coach said: “I don’t think he’ll be distracted, the guy’s a machine. Have you seen his record at international level? He’s brilliant. If you love football, you have to appreciate him … You see certain moments in certain sports. Remember the Jonah Lomu factor [in rugby union]? We’re coming through the Haaland factor at this present moment.”

Ødegaard is a doubt for the game on Thursday after a poor challenge by Bernardo Silva in the 2-1 defeat by Portugal on Sunday. “He will probably test himself a bit today,” Solbakken said of the Arsenal and Norway captain before training in the Welsh capital. “If he had no chance [of playing], he wouldn’t be here.”

Sports.title: ‘A lot of lies’: Ireland manager hits out over coverage of Bazunu exit from Israel game
Sports.content:
The Republic of Ireland manager, Heimir Hallgrímsson, has claimed “a lot of lies” were told over the goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu’s decision to withdraw from the Nations League ​game against Israel last weekend, and he does not anticipate any problems with the second match against them going ahead on Sunday.

Ireland are one of Europe’s most outspoken critics of Israel’s war in Gaza, and protests calling for the team to boycott the fixture prompted Bazunu to pull out of both games between the two countries.

The match last Sunday, which Ireland won 3-0, went ahead after a majority of their squad voted to play on the eve of the away fixture in Hungary. Media reports indicated that the squad was fractured after the meeting and vote, and that Bazunu had been insulted by teammates over his decision.

The goalkeeper is available for the home game with Austria on Thursday, but will not take part on Sunday in the rematch with Israel, which the Football Association ‌of Ireland has moved to Serbia behind closed doors.

“Gavin is a great lad, I’ve always had a good relationship with him and it’s probably tougher for him than the other players, but they have really welcomed him,” Hallgrímsson told a press conference on Wednesday.

“There’s been a lot of lies said around all of this, but we welcomed him back and he’s taking part. Amazing, I think it shows his character, as well, to be with ‌us. So I want to give him praise for that. I want to give the players praise for how welcome they have been with him,” he added. Life goes on. He’s a part of this group and I think that shows how strong the bond is between these players that even a thing like this is not breaking us.”

The Ireland midfielder Finn Azaz has also been the centre of attention given his Israeli heritage, and remained on the bench for the win against Israel. Hallgrímsson was asked if Azaz would be involved in the fixture on Sunday. “We are focusing on this one [against Austria], you can probably ask me that question later on,” the manager said.

“Finn has shown incredible emotional control and awareness. He probably is one of the people I admire the most in how he conducted himself in all of this.”

The ‌game against Austria in Dublin on Thursday is expected to bring further protests over Ireland’s decision to play Israel. Hallgrímsson said: “I am focused on football, I’ll let others think about security. The FAI has said we are playing both games and we will fulfil that. It has been really, really tough, but I surely think that in time we will have seen that we took more right decisions than wrong ones.”

Sports.title: Cristiano Ronaldo WALKS OUT on Portugal: Star, 41, leaves camp after missing training again amid row with manager and vows to 'tell the truth' in cryptic statement
Sports.content:
Cristiano Ronaldo WALKS OUT on Portugal: Star, 41, leaves camp after missing training again amid row with manager and vows to 'tell the truth' in cryptic statement

Cristiano Ronaldo has sparked claims he could retire from Portugal duty after he sensationally stormed out of Portugal's training camp amid a row with manager Jorge Jesus.

The star, 41, said in a statement on Instagram that he was heading home as a result of Jesus's comments in a tense press conference on Wednesday. It came after he failed to train with his Portugal team-mates for the third consecutive session.

Jesus appeared to have confirmed Ronaldo would not start the Nations League clash with Denmark, after the captain was left on the bench for the entirety of the 2-1 win over Norway on Sunday.

The Portugal boss, who also coached Ronaldo at Al-Nassr, admitted the player was 'angry' with him but insisted there were no issues between the two despite simmering tensions.

Ronaldo said: 'After the national team coach's press conference, and following a conversation with the President of the Portuguese Football Federation, I have decided to leave the national team training camp.

'In due time, I will tell all Portuguese people the truth about the reasons that led to my departure from the national team, to which I have always dedicated myself.

Após a conferência de imprensa do Selecionador Nacional, e no seguimento de uma conversa com o Presidente da Federação Portuguesa de Futebol, tomei a decisão de deixar o estágio da Seleção Nacional.



A seu tempo, direi a verdade a todos os Portugueses sobre as razões que… pic.twitter.com/j8Qrws9KTS — Cristiano Ronaldo (@Cristiano) September 30, 2026

Cristiano Ronaldo has confirmed he has left Portugal's camp amid a row with Jorge Jesus

'Now is the time to wish good luck to Portugal and to all my teammates.'

Portugal responded with a statement of their own, which read: 'Cristiano Ronaldo has left the national team camp. Our preparations for the next games continue with our 24 players with maximum focus on the results.'

Ronaldo had been seen leaving the Parken Stadium in Copenhagen while the rest of his team-mates trained. His private jet flew to the Danish city from Madrid and the player boarded the plane a short while after it landed.

The tension seems to have boiled over following Jesus' press conference. The manager said: 'There was no incident whatsoever.

'Any player - and I was a player myself - when you spend 20 or 30 minutes warming up and then don't get on, no-one is happy about that.

'Afterwards, as coach, I decided not to bring him on. It's nothing to make a fuss about.'

Jesus also suggested Goncalo Ramos would keep his place in the side ahead of Ronaldo for the Denmark game on Thursday. 'If I need [Ronaldo], he'll come on,' he said. 'If I don't need him, he won't.'

Ronaldo had held showdown talks with Jesus in the morning, in addition to the head of the Portuguese FA following being an unused substitute in the win over Norway.

It was the first time in 18 years that Ronaldo has not featured at all for Portugal – aside from injury or suspension absences.

At full-time on Sunday, Ronaldo stormed straight down the tunnel and did not return to thank the travelling fans alongside his team-mates.

Footage of the moment Ronaldo left the team camp has emerged on social media

Jesus had originally planned to bring on the veteran striker for a 30-minute cameo but then decided to leave him on the bench.

Reports in Portugal claimed the talks between Ronaldo and Jesus were 'calm and cordial', but his decision to leave the squad suggests otherwise.

The shocking move means that Ronaldo will not be involved in his country's next game against Denmark.

It is an inauspicious start to the relationship between Jesus and Ronaldo, who opted not to retire from international duty after the World Cup.

Only a week ago, Ronaldo reiterated his commitment to the cause, saying: 'I had a conversation with our president, with our coach (about his future).

'I still believe that I'm able to help the national team to reach what they want, and will finish when I feel like I'm not doing anything here.

'I think I can give to the national team my support, not only through the goals, but also outside of football.

'This is a new young generation. But for me the basic point is to be able on the pitch to score the goals and to help the team win games.'

Ronaldo will turn 42 in February and has scored three goals in five games for Al-Nassr so far in the Saudi Pro League this season.

Jesus and Ronaldo worked together successfully for a year when the 72-year-old was in charge of Al-Nassr but they could be on a collision course if the forward's playing time remains limited.

The 41-year-old was an unused substitute in Portugal's game with Norway on Sunday

Roberto Martinez stepped down after Portugal's 1-0 World Cup defeat by Spain and when Jesus was announced as his successor, he was asked the Ronaldo question.

Jesus insisted: 'As long as he's playing and is in a condition to be selected, I will pick him, within certain limits and under the conditions that I consider best for the national team.'

Ramos, 25, scored the winner against Norway on Sunday and is considered by many to be the natural evolution up front for Portugal.

But it seems as long as Ronaldo is around the national side, the five-time Ballon d'Or winner's playing demands will continue to be an issue for the new boss.

Sports.title: Man City's major sponsor Etihad considers legal action against Premier League after claims the airline was at the centre of 'sham' sponsorship deals
Sports.content:
Etihad Airways – the principal sponsor of Manchester City – is considering legal action against the Premier League after it was implicated in its bombshell ruling that the club breached its financial rules.

In an explosive statement, obtained by Daily Mail Sport, that further escalates the war dominating English football, the Abu Dhabi-based airline ruled to be at the centre of a series of ‘sham’ inflated sponsorship deals actually funded by City’s owners, says it ‘categorically rejects’ the findings of the competition’s commission and warns it is now seeking legal advice on next steps.

On Tuesday, the Premier League published the long-awaited, seismic verdict of an independent panel which stated that the club had disguised funding of more than £830million via a series of commercial deals between 2009 and 2018, when it won eight trophies. It found that of the £949.94m City claimed to have brought in, only £119.25m was legitimate, with the rest coming from owners the Abu Dhabi United Group and that in total it cooked the books to the tune of £900m.

While Etihad were not named in the judgement, it is the longstanding sponsor of City’s stadium, kit and training centre in a relationship with the club that stretches back to 2009. In 2011 it penned a £400m, 10-year deal that has since been extended.

City will appeal the devastating findings, in which they were found guilty on all substantive charges, and which could result in points deductions, relegation transfer bans. They have until Friday to do so.

But in another seismic development, state-owned Etihad – worth around $5billion – has now gone into battle.

The Abu Dhabi-based airline ruled to be at the centre of a series of ‘sham’ inflated sponsorship deals actually funded by City’s owners, says it ‘categorically rejects’ the verdict

They say that ‘at no time’ did the Premier League engage with them during the process and point out that they were never given a right of reply or an opportunity to ‘provide relevant information’.

They add that the ruling has ‘created damaging implications for Etihad’ and warn that the Premier League ‘must take responsibility for the consequences of the way in which these findings have been presented’.

The development came hours after Prime Minister Andy Burnham, the former mayor of Manchester, said he would be ‘really concerned to lose’ City’s owners, who have heavily invested in transforming areas of east Manchester close to the club’s stadium.

Football’s independent regulator, which has the power to kick out owners it deems unfit, said yesterday that the decision ‘raises serious issues’ and restated its powers to ‘assess the suitability of owners, directors and executives’, adding that it would ‘use these powers where appropriate’, while Burnham warned subsequently that it would be wrong to jump to conclusions.

An Etihad spokesperson said: ‘Etihad categorically rejects any finding, conclusion or implication that suggests the airline has ever been involved in improper commercial arrangements. The Premier League’s public communication of the Commission’s findings, following a period of selective leaks and reporting, has further created damaging implications for Etihad despite the airline not being named in the redacted published findings.

They added: ‘At no time did the Premier League reach out to or engage with Etihad in the process associated with the Commission’s opinion. Etihad was therefore never given the opportunity by the Premier League to be represented, to provide relevant information, or to ensure the accuracy and fairness of information relied upon in reaching conclusions that may now be interpreted as reflecting adversely on the airline.’

In what is clearly a warning to competition bosses, the statement went on: ‘Etihad is deeply concerned by the way this matter has been communicated publicly. The lack of clarity and transparency, together with the selective disclosure of information, has created damaging implications for Etihad despite the airline not being named in the published decision. The Premier League must take responsibility for the consequences of the way in which these findings have been presented.’

The spokesperson reaffirmed the airline’s commitment to City which ‘remains strong’.

‘We stand with the Club, its supporters and our wider Etihad community as Manchester City challenges the Commission’s conclusions through the processes available to it,’ it added, before concluding: ‘Etihad will seek the relevant legal counsel on the options and recourse available to protect its interests.’

Earlier, Burnham had hailed City’s owners, who arrived in 2008.

‘They’ve been such a huge partner in the building of modern Manchester,’ he added. ‘‘I do actually thank the City Football Group and the wider ownership for the money that they didn’t just put into the Etihad and the campus around it, but also into the city.’

‘I can’t intervene more in the process. It would be wrong for me to do that. It would be wrong, I think, to jump to a conclusion before having really studied all of the detail, but obviously it’s ongoing, and because it’s still contested by Manchester City, then I think it’s right that I don’t say much more.’

Burnham, an avid Everton supporter, campaigned for his club when they fell foul of the Premier League’s spending rules in 2023-24.

‘I remember people proclaiming Everton guilty at the time,’ he said, ‘and with hindsight, I think more people would say that wasn’t fair the way that was handled. So it would be wrong of me to leap to one side given the experience that I’d had before becoming prime minister.’

The Premier League has been contacted for comment.

Sports.title: Ricky Hatton left £30MILLION estate after his tragic death, new figures reveal, as son Campbell claims family are 'completely in the dark' amid dispute over late boxer's finances
Sports.content:
Ricky Hatton left £30MILLION estate after his tragic death, new figures reveal, as son Campbell claims family are 'completely in the dark' amid dispute over late boxer's finances

Ricky Hatton reportedly amassed a £30million fortune before his death last year, though uncertainty remains over how the boxing legend's estate will be distributed.

Hatton, who died aged 46 last September, won multiple world titles before using his fight earnings to build a business empire worth more than £20million, with at least another £10m tied up in property investments, according to The Sun.

Trustees were appointed to manage Hatton's estate after he took his own life in September last year.

However, sources close to the family claim communication with the trustees has since broken down, with one describing the situation as a 'complete mess', according to an earlier report in The Sun.

It was thought Hatton had intended for his fortune to pass to his three children, Campbell, 25, and daughters Millie, 14, and Fearne, 12. However, a year after his death, the family are still waiting to learn how and when the estate will be distributed.

Campbell told The Sun on Wednesday: 'My family is still completely in the dark. We’ve had no involvement in my dad’s finances for over 15 years.'

Hatton, who died aged 46 last September, won multiple world titles before using his fight earnings to build a business and property empire

It was thought Hatton had intended for his fortune to pass to his three children, Campbell, 25 (above), and daughters Millie, 14, and Fearne, 12

During his successful boxing career, Hatton used his fight earnings to finance a string of businesses, many of them linked to property investments in his hometown of Hyde, as well as in Leicestershire, London and Kent.

One source said Hatton was 'determined to ensure that he had a financial legacy from his incredible career'.

'Everyone who knew and loved Ricky would give anything to have him back. But during his life he's done a great job of providing for the people he loved the most, his children,' the source added.

Earlier this month, the Daily Mail reported that Hatton's house had been sold for £1.5m this year after £350,000 was knocked off the original asking price.

The house, where Hatton was found in September last year, was put up for sale shortly before his death for £1.85million but was later taken off the market following his tragic death.

The mansion then went back on offer for £1.75million, then £1.65million before it was sold for £1.5million.

It was described by the estate agent as being a 'landmark modern residence offering luxury, space and unrivalled lifestyle features'.

It said that the five-bedroom six-bathroom property, which was built in 2010, had been 'impeccably designed'.

One source said Hatton was 'determined to ensure that he had a financial legacy from his incredible career'

Hatton put his own stamp on the property, decorating it with personal touches including a traditional telephone box in the garden and an array of Manchester City memorabilia. Among its more unusual features are seats salvaged from the club's former Maine Road stadium.

It has extensive landscaped grounds with greenbelt views, plus a leisure suite with a heated indoor pool and jacuzzi.

A private gym and cinema room complement a games room and bar area, which is separated from the pool by a striking glass wall.

The principal bedroom suite features a walk-in dressing room, a luxurious en suite bathroom, a crushed-velvet chaise longue and dark patterned wallpaper.

Elsewhere, the property offers multiple reception rooms and expansive open-plan living areas centred around a high-specification, dark-panelled kitchen.

Situated in the sought-after area of Gee Cross in Greater Manchester, the estate is equipped with advanced security features, including CCTV.

The estate agents said: 'This is a rare opportunity to acquire a truly outstanding home in one of the North West's most prestigious and sought-after residential locations.'

For confidential support, call Samaritans on 116 123, visit samaritans.org or visit thecalmzone.net/get-support.

Sports.title: Moment Arsenal star Leah Williamson concedes bizarre penalty after handling the ball in the area as Gunners throw away two-goal lead against Paris FC
Sports.content:
Leah Williamson gave away a bizarre penalty as Arsenal threw away a two-goal lead to draw with Paris FC in the Women's Champions League.

Renee Slegers' side have struggled to find the back of the net this season, but Alessia Russo ended her goalscoring drought with a clinical finish in the 41st minute.

Georgia Stanway then joined her Lioness team-mate in getting her first goal of the campaign in the 50th minute, her first since signing for the north London club from Bayern Munich in the summer.

But Paris FC bided their time, scoring a wonderful goal on the counter 20 minutes later before a miscommunication between Williamson and Arsenal goalkeeper Misa Rodriguez led to a penalty in the 87th minute.

It appeared Williamson thought Rodriguez had thrown her the ball, and she handled it to place it on the edge of the six-yard box to take the goal kick herself.

The problem was that Rodriguez had in fact kicked the ball to Williamson and, with play considered live, the referee judged it to be handball and pointed to the penalty spot.

WOW! What on earth has happened here? 😮



Arsenal's Leah Williamson concedes a bizarre penalty to give Paris FC a penalty 👀



📺 Watch the UEFA Women’s Champions League live on @DisneyPlusUK pic.twitter.com/T3MWzaFzAC — ESPN UK (@ESPNUK) September 30, 2026

Arsenal vice-captain Leah Williamson gave away a bizarre penalty as Arsenal threw away a two-goal lead to draw with Paris FC in the Women's Champions League

According to IFAB's Laws of the Game, a goal kick is in play once the ball is stationary and 'is kicked from any point within the goal area by a player of the defending team'. Replays showed the ball had come to a stop after Rodriguez threw it onto the pitch before kicking it to Williamson, meaning the referee's decision was correct.

Williamson looked visibly devastated by the incident as Maeline Mendy stepped up to convert the equaliser.

After the match, Slegers came under scrutiny for choosing to skip the post-match press conference, instead sending assistant coach Aaron D'Antino to meet the media.

D'Antino said: 'We didn’t think it was a penalty, we don’t think the goal kick had actually been taken for what we had seen. But it goes to VAR and apparently that’s a penalty.

'It's just passing the ball to Leah from what I remember seeing, the ball was still rolling and she was moving it to Leah for her to take the goal kicks as we normally do.'

Slegers is under pressure heading into this weekend's match against champions Manchester City, with Arsenal having won just one of their opening four WSL games and only managing a narrow 1-0 win in their Champions League opener against HB Koge last week.

After making statement signings in the summer, including star midfielder Stanway and World Cup winner Ona Batlle, Arsenal were widely expected to challenge for the title this season.

They are now seven points behind league leaders City, and defeat at the weekend could effectively end their title hopes before the race has properly begun.

Sports.title: Dock points for NINE years, force Abu Dhabi owners to sell up and a walk of shame down to League TWO: Our experts have their say on Man City's fate after club found guilty of £900m 'sham'
Sports.content:
English football was left stunned on Tuesday with the verdict that Manchester City cooked the books to the tune of £900m in a nine-year period peppered with ‘sham’ sponsorship deals, all in a bid to pump money into the club and swerve Premier League spending rules. City were found guilty of ‘all charges related to serious breaches’ of the regulations and the majority of those in relation to its failure to co-operate with the competition’s probe. The club will appeal against the verdict, but with a sanctions hearing due before that appeal is heard, our experts have their say on what the punishment should be... IAN HERBERT: The owners must be forced to sell... but rivals should say no to compensation The Premier League should relegate Manchester City and make the provision for them to face a 20-point deduction in each of the next three seasons. Fines and points deductions will be immaterial to them and straight relegation would mean them enjoying a joyful next campaign thumping everyone in the Championship. That should not be permissible. City’s typically aggressive response on Tuesday – alleging bias against them by describing the adjudication panel as a ‘Premier League commission’ – should be deemed an aggravating factor, as should another drawn-out appeal, were that to fail. The Independent Football Regulator must force a sale of the club whose Abu Dhabi owners have brought British football into disrepute and breached a signed undertaking to run City with integrity. The club should be stripped of their titles. For the benefit of the game, other clubs should sign an amnesty agreement, agreeing not to further line lawyers' pockets by seeking compensation. City chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak and CEO Ferran Soriano have both pleaded the club's innocence OLIVER HOLT: Start again in League Two - and yes, they should be stripped of titles Like a lot of people, I suspect, my views on what should happen to City are hardening as new details of their wrong-doing are released. The scale of it emphasises the extent of the advantage they gained. It also emphasises how difficult it was for those abiding by the rules to compete with City. If City's appeal fails, they should be expelled from the Premier League and made to start again in League Two. Instinctively, I don't like the idea of stripping a club of titles won but I don't see any alternative in this case. The fault in those punishments is that the fans, who are blameless in all this, pay the price. But the ownership should be made to pay a price, too. They cannot be allowed to remain as custodians of a great club they have brought so low. TOM COLLOMOSSE: Guarantee relegation - then make the system fairer Speed is essential here. For too long, too many commentators have responded to every development in this saga with ‘Oh, it will take years.’ Enough of that, for Goodness sake. We have already taken far too much time to reach this point and waiting for more months or – God forbid – years for the outcome will do untold damage, not only to the Premier League but to English football. Of course, Manchester City have the right to appeal. But if someone is found guilty of a crime, the sentence arrives before the appeal. If the opposite happens in this case, it will lead only to more chaos. Sergio Aguero's famous goal against QPR in 2012 gave City their first league title since 1968

Your browser does not support iframes.

The punishment should come swiftly and should be a points deduction this season large enough that relegation is virtually guaranteed. That should be followed by a points deduction next season, and a fixed compensation bill to all affected clubs – as proposed by former Aston Villa CEO Christian Purslow. This is far more effective than stripping titles. Finally, we need a more equitable system of financial rules. It feels uncomfortable that clubs like Tottenham and Manchester United can underperform season on season yet continue to spend vast sums on transfers just because they generate huge revenue off the pitch. A fairer system will go a long way to stopping any repeat of the Manchester City case. KIERAN GILL: One big points deduction... and a multi-window transfer ban If Manchester City are to win on appeal, it needs to be based on the actual evidence, not on them trying to find a technicality to do with impartiality or whatever else they can conjure. Their reputation is already in the mud after that verdict from the independent commission. Their only way back is by winning fairly; not by continuing to try to thwart the investigation. If their guilt is upheld, then they should not be a Premier League club for at least one season. So in my mind, a hefty points deduction, circa 60-70 points, would be sufficient for a start. Along with a multi-window transfer ban, the stripping of the titles won (they would be tainted anyway and I would not re-allocate those titles to the runners-up), and I could not see how their ownership could remain the same. Too harsh? If ultimately guilty, City will have been found to have deliberately sabotaged so many years of football for not only their own supporters but us all. LEWIS STEELE: Dock points for nine years... and City's current stars need answers They should be docked points nine years in a row (given that’s how many years they were cheating for). A simple relegation is like a slap on the wrist: they would waltz the Championship and be fighting for Europe again within 18 months. Elliot Anderson is among the Man City stars who may want answers from the club's ownership They have duped their rivals for a decade so should be punished accordingly. City fans — many of whom are in denial — are right to feel aggrieved but their anger should not be directed at the Premier League but the men that have run their club into the ground. I also feel sorry for the likes of Enzo Maresca, Elliot Anderson, Enzo Fernandez etc — the people who have just joined the club and been lied to by the owners (it seems). Surely they have a claim? MATT BARLOW: Play in the Championship next season - and put an asterisk next to all their titles Cheating on such a vast and systematic scale demands a severe penalty with sporting consequences. Otherwise, what’s the point of anybody following the rules? Money is no object to Manchester City’s owners. It defies the essence of sport if they can effectively pay to play by different rules. City should be expelled from the Premier League and all the titles won during the contaminated era should be asterisked. Swindon were denied entry to the top flight in 1990 for breaking financial rules. I’m not sure how Chelsea escaped sporting penalty for their recent case, but that’s another story. City should start next season in the Championship. I can't see a point in sinking them any further down the EFL food chain just to watch them squirm. But all future accounts should be subject to scrutiny by football's authorities to make sure they do not reoffend. I don't think we should start meddling to redistribute titles, for where does that begin and end? But I expect there will be clubs seeking compensation. It's easy to see why they will be aggrieved but at the same time a very depressing prospect. Man City could be playing in the second tier for the first time since the 2001-02 season, when Eyal Berkovic and Shaun Goater were part of the squad which won promotion as champions RIATH AL-SAMARRAI: Repay the rest of the pyramid by putting them in League Two How to solve a problem like Manchester City? Turn them into a solution. To my mind, one season to the Championship isn’t severe enough for cheating that stretched across nine and has had residual benefits up to the present day. So here’s an idea: a walk of shame to match the sham and one that feeds a financial boost to the lowest reaches of the pyramid. The thought hinges on expulsion from the Premier League, if the guilty verdict remains intact after the appeals process. Measures could be taken in the interim to prevent a tainted champion for 2026-27, such as a severe points deduction, with the expulsion occurring next summer (an optimistic timeline, perhaps). The question then would be one of where to insert the club, which falls on the EFL. My suggestion is an immediate drop to League Two, guaranteeing City spend at least three seasons in the EFL before securing enough promotions to return to the Premier League. The interest in the EFL in that period will be huge, as will the financial reward for each club they visit on their way back.

Sports.title: Boxing chief Turki Alalshikh calls out Dua Lipa in bizarre rant about pop sensation during Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua press conference
Sports.content:
Boxing chief Turki Alalshikh has claimed that Dua Lipa has refused to perform at the Tyson Fury v Anthony Joshua super-fight in a bizarre tirade against the pop sensation during the launch press conference.

On Wednesday evening, Britain's two most iconic boxers of the last two decades went face to face for the first time since their eagerly anticipated clash was announced last week.

Ahead of the press conference, Alalshikh, who was lauded by Fury, Joshua and many others during the evening for financing the fight, was invited to speak about how the 'Battle of Britain' came to be.

New York's Madison Square Garden and Wembley had previously been billed as potential venues for the 'super' heavyweight clash, but it has since been confirmed that the Principality Stadium in Cardiff, Wales, will host the contest.

During his explanation of how the venue was eventually decided, Alalshikh took a swipe at Dua Lipa in the process.

He said: 'I will be honest today, I know that London wouldn't give me the stadium until 2am, and I know that Dua Lipa will not perform in the stadium, because she doesn't like boxing, and maybe she doesn't like me.'

Turki Alalshikh went on a bizarre tirade during Tyson Fury v Anthony Joshua press conference

The boxing chief claimed that Dua Lipa has turned down the chance to perform ahead of the long-awaited bout

Dua Lipa's representatives have been approached for comment by Daily Mail Sport.

Alalshikh went on to also explain the financial losses that staging the bout in Britain has led to.

He added: 'Nobody questioned me about UK. I love the British people, I try to deliver everything for them. Put yourself in my shoes; there's a situation to lose $70million (£52.8m); the best is to have it in a good time zone.

'I have two reasons, and I know London won't deliver it; they won't give me the stadium until 2am... Wales delivered it; it's still the UK, the town of Ryan Giggs, let's do it.'

Anthony Joshua's promoter Eddie Hearn has been vocal about his and the two-time heavyweight world champion's desire to have the fight staged in the UK.

The chairman of Matchroom took his moment on stage at the British Airways ARC to thank the British boxing community for applying the 'pressure' to ensure the fight is played out on British soil.

Fury and Joshua faced off for the first time ahead of their super fight on Wednesday evening

'I'm excited,' Hearn said. 'Turki, I know we've fallen out, but I promise you this'll be the greatest night you've ever had in boxing.

'On a serious note, when we talked about this fight, you envisaged it for British boxing. This guy (Joshua) has changed boxing in this country. So has Tyson Fury. We are the envy of the boxing world.

'We can't stage it anywhere else. Thank you to the British public for putting the pressure on. We couldn't do it, we failed.'

Sports.title: Golf star Phil Mickelson checked into addiction treatment facility because of 'family trauma'
Sports.content:
Golf star Phil Mickelson checked into addiction treatment facility because of 'family trauma'

Phil Mickelson entered an addiction treatment center amid ongoing personal issues, according to a report.

The professional golfer, 56, is said to have checked into the undisclosed facility recently to seek 'treatment for family trauma and addiction,' a spokesperson for Mickelson told TMZ.

The six-time major champion, who has previously opened up on his struggles with a gambling addiction, is believed to have already left the center.

The Daily Mail has contacted Mickelson's representatives for comment.

The news comes after Mickelson stepped away from professional golf on the LIV Golf circuit and at this year's major championships.

He missed the start of the LIV Golf season, returned for one tournament in South Africa in March, but then stepped away again, even pulling out of the Masters and the Open Championship.

Phil Mickelson entered an addiction treatment center amid ongoing personal issues

Mickelson is pictured with his wife, Amy, at the 2012 Ryder Cup gala in Illinois

At the time, Mickelson cited an unspecified private family matter involving his wife, Amy, for his absence.

Mickelson has been married to Amy, 54, for almost 30 years after tying the knot back in November 1996. The couple share three children together in Evan, Sophie and Amanda.

The left-handed legend has been candid about his struggles with gambling, previously opening up on his addiction in 2023.

He said at the time that he had 'crossed the line from moderation into addiction which isn't fun at all.'

'The money wasn't ever the issue since our financial security has never been threatened, but I was so distracted I wasn't able to be present with the ones I love and caused a lot of harm,' he said.

He also described how this 'lack of presence' has been 'so hurtful' for his family, saying he's been 'often' told throughout his addiction, 'You're here, but you're not with us.'

'It affected those I care about in ways I wasn't aware or could fully understand,' Mickelson said. 'It's like a hurricane is going on outside and I'm isolated in a shelter oblivious to what was happening.'

'When I came out there was so much damage to clean up that I just wanted to back inside and not deal with it,' he added.

The golf icon has been married to wife Amy for close to 30 years. They share three children

Mickelson and Amy are pictured with their children, Evan, Sophie and Amanda, after his victory at the 2013 Open Championship

Mickelson has also made headlines this year for a series of alleged scandals and bombshell sexual misconduct accusations.

In June, Golf Digest reported that Mickelson had been removed as a member of The Farms Golf Club in Rancho Santa Fe, California, amid allegations of inappropriate physical contact with a female staff member.

According to multiple sources, Mickelson approached the employee in the clubhouse, made non-consensual and inappropriate physical contact with her, and he was confronted by club officials mid-round before being told to vacate the premises.

A representative confirmed he had resigned from the club.

A separate report from Skratch later painted the incidents as part of a deeply entrenched pattern of behavior. Mickelson had previously departed two other high-end clubs - the Madison Club and The Bridges, also in Rancho Santa Fe - with sources at both allegedly saying personal conduct was a primary factor.

Mickelson hit back at the allegations through his attorney, Tom Clare, at the time.

'There is a great deal of misinformation circulating and, while Phil's full attention is devoted to a private family health matter, he has retained defamation counsel and is determined to hold accountable any publication or individual trafficking in speculation or false rumors,' Clare said in a statement.

Mickelson's spokespeople also claimed that he has 'never been expelled from a golf club' and that the decision to leave said clubs was 'his alone.'

The golfer and his wife are seen taking in the action on the Sunday of the 2021 Ryder Cup

Mickelson was accused of showing a photo of himself naked and erect to Ashley Perez (left) in 2015, then-wife of fellow golfer Pat Perez

Just over a week later, however, Mickelson was accused of showing a nude photo to a fellow professional's wife in a bombshell report on his private life published by Skratch - written by legendary golf writer Alan Shipnuck.

In the piece, Mickelson is accused of allegedly showing a naked photograph of himself with an erect penis to the then-wife of fellow Tour professional Pat Perez during a tournament in 2015.

Ashley Perez, who was married to Pat from 2014 to 2023, told the outlet the incident occurred during the Barclays tournament in New Jersey, when Mickelson arranged for the couple to join him at his villa at Liberty National Golf Course.

While Pat had excused himself to use the restroom, leaving Ashley and Mickelson alone on the patio, she claims the six-time major champion produced his phone and showed her a full-body image of himself naked and aroused.

'Phil says to me, 'I'm going to leave my bedroom door open tonight. When Pat falls asleep I want you to come see me',' Ashley told Shipnuck.

According to the outlet, she said she declined his advances and did not immediately tell her husband, saying she had not wanted to create a scene mid-tournament.

When Perez was eventually told, he confronted Mickelson - who the outlet reports ultimately apologized during a corporate outing at the Madison Club in La Quinta, California.

The allegation became central to Perez's now-notorious comments on Claude Harmon's podcast in November 2022, when he said: 'I have a different hate for Phil than most people.

Ashley Perez told Skratch that Mickelson apologized during an awkward 26-minute call

'Phil crossed the line with me that is just uncrossable and unforgivable. He knows that he screwed up. He apologized for the action, but I cannot forgive him for it.'

Ashley Perez says she has a recording of a subsequent 26-minute phone call between Pat and Mickelson. During it, she claims, Mickelson alternated between contrition and saying he could not remember the details of the evening. Shipnuck also reports he has listened to the recording.

When Pat told him he had shown Ashley 'a naked photo', Mickelson is alleged to have responded: 'You mean topless?'

Without fully admitting what had happened, Mickelson is said to have told the couple: 'I can't tell you how disgusted and embarrassed I am in myself.'

A spokesperson for the golfer told the Daily Mail earlier this year: 'Some of the allegations circulating about Mr. Mickelson are false, and others revisit mistakes he has already acknowledged, publicly or privately. Stacking the disputed claims next to the ones he has owned does not make them credible. It instead contributes to a false and misleading narrative.

'No person, no article, and no book can present an accurate, complete, or personal story of the life Mr. Mickelson and his family have lived. His story, struggles, and recovery belong to him and to the people who have shared it closely alongside him.

'Recovery is not a straight line. Throughout their 35-year relationship, his wife, Amy Mickelson, has supported Mr. Mickelson and their family with extraordinary grace, unwavering love, and the belief that people are measured not only by their failures, but by what they do to make them right.

'Mr. Mickelson's priority is to become the husband, father, and man his family deserves. Right now, that means giving his full attention to a private family health matter. He understands that parts of his life are public, but his family's private matters are not.'

Sports.title: Anthony Joshua reveals that Tyson Fury's estranged uncle has joined his camp ahead of £150m mega-fight as Gypsy King claims: 'I've not spoken to him for years'
Sports.content:
Anthony Joshua reveals that Tyson Fury's estranged uncle has joined his camp ahead of £150m mega-fight as Gypsy King claims: 'I've not spoken to him for years'

Anthony Joshua made the startling revelation that he has joined forces with Tyson Fury's uncle, Peter, ahead of their eagerly-anticipated super-fight in Cardiff in December.

Never has the calling of a sporting press conference agitated as much, if not more, attention than the event itself.

Without putting Fury and Joshua into the same room in London on Wednesday evening there would have been no chance of them sharing a ring in Cardiff two months from now.

Never has a promo prompted so many startling revelations, either. We might never have known that Fury’s estranged uncle is advising AJ on how to prevent Tyson beating him. Traveller families are usually bonded by such fierce loyalties that we can only wonder about the tensions around the camp fire.

‘Not to worry,’ said the Gypsy King about the defection. ‘I haven’t spoken to him for years.’

Nor might we have learned that Joshua took a mind-blowing pay cut in order to haul the Battle of Britain back home from the clutches of New York.

Even though the ritual stare down was lengthy the chatter was amicable and ended in smiles

When they took to the stage there were very few of the histrionics which are the trademark of most of Tyson Fury’s ticket-selling appearances

How much of a purse deduction? ‘Twelve figures’ declared his promoter Eddie Hearn. That’s £10million at least.

AJ shrugged and cited another fringe benefit picked up during the maelstrom of doubt as to whether this fight between a pair of British world heavyweight champions would ever take place. He also added Fury’s former trainer Ben Davison to his team.

Joshua said: ‘Ben’s pinpointing details which will make the difference on the night.’

Fury replied: ‘Ben can’t put muscles on that suspect chin.’

He could not resist reminding everyone that Davison has just returned from Las Vegas where he presided over Conor Benn’s two-round devastation by America’s great Latin hope, Ryan Garcia.

When they took to the stage there were very few of the histrionics which are the trademark of most of Fury’s ticket-selling appearances.

Instead he advertised ‘probably the greatest fight boxing’s ever seen if you factor in the commercial aspect'.

Which includes the US$150million split equally between the two of them as they put an end to 12 years of public waiting for this fight.

Joshua said: ‘Both of us want to do British boxing proud.’

Even though the ritual stare down was lengthy the chatter was amicable and ended in smiles with Fury inviting Joshua to ‘a pint of Guinness as soon as the fight over, win lose or draw'.

Well, they are ten weeks away from them putting on their fight faces.

Sports.title: Man City charges LIVE: Jurgen Klopp speaks, Pep Guardiola statement, punishment latest
Sports.content:
The latest news on Manchester City's charges after the club were found guilty of alleged breaches of Premier League financial rules

Hello and welcome to Mirror Football's Manchester City charges live blog for Wednesday, September 30.

The Premier League officially announced the club's guilty verdict on 114 breaches of financial rules on Tuesday afternoon, four days after media reports broke the news.

A statement from the league read: "An independent Commission has found Manchester City FC guilty of all charges related to serious breaches of the Premier League’s financial rules over a nine-season period, and the majority of charges in relation to its failure to co-operate with the League’s investigation."

As a result, City have until Friday to appeal the decision, which the club are likely to do as they continue to protest their innocence.

Manchester City also released a statement of their own in the wake of the Premier League's confirmation. It read: "Manchester City FC is both disappointed and surprised by the opinion of the Premier League Commission, that has been published today.

"The Club is innocent of the accusations made by the Premier League and a comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence exists in support of all of its positions, relating to this case. The Club will therefore be relentless, and where necessary proactive, in any and all appropriate regulatory and legal forums.

"The Premier League process remains ongoing, with significant elements uncompleted. Manchester City FC will now pursue the appeal avenues open to it, on the basis that the opinion contains clear material errors, of law, principle and fact, and is unsafe.

"The Club has diligently respected due process for eight years on the basis that the Premier League Board and Executive would behave as an independent, impartial and fair-minded regulator, free from partisan influence. The Club is obviously restricted in what it can say further until all future proceedings are complete."

Stay tuned for the latest news and updates in our live blog below as the saga continues to unfold...

Sports.title: Tyson Fury's uncle helping Anthony Joshua prepare to fight bitter rival
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury's uncle helping Anthony Joshua prepare to fight bitter rival

Joshua, 36, and Fury, 38, faced off for the first time ahead of their £150million heavyweight showdown in Cardiff on December 11

View Image Anthony Joshua is being helped by Peter Fury

Anthony Joshua has claimed even Tyson Fury's own FAMILY want him to lose the biggest fight of his career.

‌



Joshua, 36, and Fury, 38, faced off for the first time ahead of their £150million heavyweight showdown in Cardiff on December 11. And Joshua revealed he has been taking advice from Fury's uncle Peter who led his nephew to his first world title. The pair split after Fury defeated Wladimir Klitschko in 2015 and Joshua said: "I speak to Peter. He's willing to help me as well.

‌



"He has given me ideas about our training and about how I can approach the fight. Everybody wants me to win and everybody's going to tell me how to win." Joshua has also reunited with trainer Ben Davison who was instrumental in guiding Fury out of his drink-and-drug fuelled depression and back to the ring.

‌



Tyson Fury accuses Anthony Joshua of trying to CANCEL box-office fight for petty reason READ MORE :

Davison helped Fury to a draw with Deontay Wilder in 2018 and oversaw wins over Otto Wallin and Tom Schwarz but was then dumped before his charge became world champion again by stopping Wilder in 2020.

Joshua worked with Davison for his wins over Otto Wallin and Francis Ngannou before he was knocked out by Daniel Dubois two years ago, leading to the pair splitting. But Davison is now back in Joshua's corner and he added: "I'm at a stage in my life now where everybody better shut up and listen to me when it comes to boxing because I've learned more than most people and most coaches now.

Article continues below

"When I sat back and I observed this, I realised Ben Davison will be a big addition to this fight with what he can add to helping me beat Tyson Fury. He's very good at pinpointing certain things leading up to a fight that I can execute and exploit. I believe Ben Davison will get me that one step closer to landing the perfect punch to pin Fury to the ground."

Fury, who is now trained by SugarHill Steward added: "I left Ben Davison to go with Sugar Hill because he wasn't good enough and this is the same Ben Davison who Anthony Joshua left because he wasn't good enough. That gives me encouragement and that gives me happiness. He'll probably go out there, get told to throw a jab and throw an uppercut and get himself chinned."
