Sports.title: Cristiano Ronaldo LEAVES Portugal camp after crisis meeting with manager as statement issued
Sports.content:
Cristiano Ronaldo LEAVES Portugal camp after crisis meeting with manager as statement issued

Cristiano Ronaldo's falling out with Portugal manager Jorge Jesus has resulted in his dramatic decision to walk away from the national team in the middle of the current break

View 3 Images Ronaldo was left on the bench against Norway (Image: Getty Images)

Cristiano Ronaldo has decided to walk away from Portugal, potentially bringing to an end his storied international career.

‌



Ronaldo met with Portugal manager Jorge Jesus in a hastily arranged crisis meeting on Wednesday after being left furious at not playing in their 2-1 win over Norway on Sunday.

‌



The talks did not go well and the 41-year-old Al-Nassr striker has walked away from the national team in the middle of the international break.

‌



He wrote on Instagram: "After the press conference of the national team, and following a conversation with the President of the Portuguese Football Federation, I have decided to leave the national team.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



"In time, I will tell all the Portuguese the truth about the reasons that motivated me to leave the national team, to which I always devoted myself. Now is the time to wish Portugal and all my teammates good luck, without exception."

Ronaldo's bombshell post came shortly after Jesus held a press conference and told reporters there was no issue between him and Portugal's all-time record goalscorer.

"There was no incident whatsoever," he said. "Any player - and I was a player myself - when you spend 20 or 30 minutes warming up and then don't get on, no-one is happy about that."

‌



View 3 Images Jorge Jesus has owned his decision not to play Cristiano Ronaldo against Norway (Image: Patricia de Melo Moreira / AFP via Getty Images)

Explaining the situation further, he added: "Afterwards, as coach, I decided not to bring him on. It's nothing to make a fuss about."

“The way I was reading the game (against Norway), he didn’t come on," he said. “Because it’s not Cristiano, just like it will never be any player that will change my ideas as the coach. Never! “Not him, not anyone in football. Not him, not anyone, not any president. Never! Zero!”

‌



Jesus started with Goncalo Ramos against Norway and the AC Milan striker scored the winning goal to continue their perfect start to the Nations League. The former Benfica boss has said Ramos would start the next match against Denmark.

Ronaldo recently revealed that he considered his future in international football following Portugal's defeat by Spain in the last 16 of the World Cup. He ultimately decided to carry on after veteran coach Jesus took over from Roberto Martinez, but their relationship has brought about the end of his international career on 234 caps, with 146 goals.

Jesus was forced to explain why Ronaldo walked straight down the tunnel following the win over Norway. "I did not realise he was upset," he said post-match.

‌



"Only he can answer that. What is certain is that not playing him does not mean I do not rely on him. In fact, before the match, I told him: 'I will not start you, but I will bring you on as a substitute.' This is football."

View 3 Images Ronaldo stormed away from the pitch after Portgual's win against Norway (Image: Getty Images)

Ronaldo's shock announcement comes just a week after he explained his burning motivation to continue playing international football.

Article continues below

“I had a conversation with our president, with our coach," he said. "I still believe that I’m able to help the national team to reach what they want, and will finish when I feel like I’m not doing anything here.

“I think I can give to the national team my support, not only through the goals, but also outside of football. This is a new young generation. But for me the basic point is to be able on the pitch to score the goals and to help the team win games.”

Sports.title: Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua share intense face-off ahead of mega fight
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua share intense face-off ahead of mega fight

Anthony Joshua and Tyson Fury will clash in Cardiff and December and came face to face tonight after weeks of rowing over their all-British heavyweight showdown

View Image Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua face off ahead of their fight (Image: Getty Images)

Anthony Joshua and Tyson Fury stood nose-to-nose tonight following a rather respectful press conference ahead of their mega-fight.

‌



The British heavyweights will finally meet in the ring in Cardiff on December 11, a decade after their rivalry began. At one point last week, the fight looked to be in jeopardy once again as rows erupted over the involvement of UFC chief Dana White and when Fury was due to begin drug-testing.

‌



But Fury was tested at his hotel this morning and White was not present at the press conference and face-off which saw both men refuse to blink.

‌



In a rather intense and stone-cold face-off, Joshua broke the ice a little bit towards the end after tickling his upcoming rival - with Fury seeing the funny side of it. Security were not needed on this occasion, but despite their rather friendly encounter, tempers nearly flared during the launch press conference in London on Wednesday evening.

FOLLOW OUR FIGHTING FB PAGE! Latest boxing and MMA news, analysis and much more via our dedicated Facebook page

Fury, 38, was quick to throw a jibe at Joshua and promoter Eddie Hearn after 'AJ' dubbed himself the 'landlord' in the build-up to Wednesday's meeting. "In the build-up, they talked about landlords, the Dom Perrignons, the guvnors... When I look behind me, I only see one don, Fury v AJ, I ain't paying, son," he said.

‌



“I don’t make a thing about this bulls***, but when I walk out, it’s Tyson Fury against his opponent, I thought I’d highlight that. Eddie Hearn is just a sausage." But Fury did double down on his offer after stating he would go for a pint with Hearn and Joshua after December's dust-up.

“I’ve never won a world title here [in the UK], just remember GK is No 1, the boss. Eddie don’t like that, he don’t like that. I haven’t got a problem with Eddie, I’d go for a pint with Eddie, he’s been a good promoter, he’s sung your praises. But he’s been crying." said Fury.

How to buy tickets for Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua fight READ MORE :

Joshua got under his rival's skin a tad after revealing that he received a call asking if it would be possible to have his name second on the official fight poster. “I got a call saying, ‘do you mind if Fury’s name is first?’ I said ‘yes, I don’t want to lose the fight,'" he admitted. An irate Fury was quick to hit back: “Bulls***.”

‌



But apart from a few insults hurled here and there, the pair were rather respectful towards each other and played their part in a rather cordial press conference. As the two men faced off in the middle of the stage, Turki Alalshikh stood behind the two behemoths with an official 'Battle of Britain' belt - highlighting the importance of the showdown.

The pair have the chance to bring even more hardware home and add to their respective trophy cabinets after it was reported that they will meet for the WBA 'super' heavyweight title.

And in a bid to become a three-time world champion, Fury was eager to give away the gameplan for his fight with Joshua, revealing: “I’m going to come out, blast him out of there, it’ll be gunfight at the O.K. Corral. I’m not going to box, I’m going to throw down, I’ll catch him, and when I do, it’ll be curtains. That’s it.”

Sports.title: Thomas Tuchel sends brutal reality check over England finding Harry Kane replacement
Sports.content:
Thomas Tuchel sends brutal reality check over England finding Harry Kane replacement

Harry Kane chalked up international goal number 87 during the Three Lions' win in Prague, with Thomas Tuchel warning it's a waste of time trying to find a replacement

View 4 Images England manager Thomas Tuchel and captain Harry Kane

Thomas Tuchel has warned England will never have another Harry Kane.

‌



Kane, 33, is just 13 goals away from reaching 100 for England and will go down as the nation’s greatest-ever striker. England captain Kane is also just two caps from equalling Peter Shilton’s record of 125 appearances.

‌



It was Tuchel who was manager when Bayern Munich signed Kane in 2023 and club legend Ali Hoeness even called him “Bayern’s greatest-ever signing.”

‌



Kane is always chasing records and needs just 13 goals to reach the century landmark. Tuchel said: “He is closing in. He scored again. 13 left. That’s 13 matches.”

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



A while ago, it looked like a dream for Kane to reach 100. Now it looks just a matter of time or just another 13 games, according to Tuchel. England boss Tuchel has a special bond with Kane as captain and manager but also they have become close and reliant on each other.

Kane sets the tone, is the voice in the dressing room and Tuchel also says that he sets the tone with his hunger and desire and training. That is also what makes him a great striker.

Tuchel said: “What is there to say? He does it in every single match. The highest level of goalscorer, of finishing.

‌



“You were there for maybe the first 15 minutes open training session on a minus two and he is on the second lap over on the left at the front. He is not behind, he is not slow, he is not doing his shoes.

View 4 Images Kane scored England goal 87 during the win over Czechia

“He is the first one out there and then we play some little boxes in training, he is the first one to push everyone and that is his mindset and he became a very, very hard-working forward on top of his finishing skills. He is a complete package.”

‌



Kane is also red-hot favourite to win the Ballon d’Or after his 73 goal haul last season for club and country which helped Bayern win the Treble.

The England striker has become a legend in Germany and Tuchel is full of pride to see him do so well for Bayern, even being labelled their greatest-ever signing.

Tuchel said: “That is so beautiful as it tells me everyone can see his true value and his personality and that he imposed that into a big club like Bayern Munich and he gets the full praise for it and that is very, very impressive.

‌



“It is not easy to change and to come to Bayern Munich when you win, win, win and it is a big club. You are under the spotlight and he won everyone over with his quality, work ethic and his personality. It is a beautiful story.”

View 4 Images The Bayern forward is the red-hot favourite to win the Ballon d'Or

But the bigger issue for England is how do you replace Kane? There is no obvious candidate. Dominic Calvert-Lewin is in this squad and is surely the closest but it feels impossible to step into the shoes of a national treasure.

‌



There is also an amazing stat the only English striker under the age of 27 to score a Champions League goal is Liam Delap. It is a worry.

But Tuchel believes it is a waste of time trying to replace him - and England need to find different solutions. Jude Bellingham virtually played up front in a 4-4-2 in the World Cup and came on up front against Czech Republic.

Tuchel added: “You will not get another Harry Kane, first of all. We look for different options and solutions. We finished the game with Jude up front as a No 9.

‌



“There will be someone else but it will not be Harry or a copy of Harry. We will find a solution when it comes to it but maybe not me. It might be another 10 years.

View 4 Images Tuchel has said it could take 10 years to replace England's talismanic striker (Image: Justin Setterfield/Getty Images)

“I like Jude as a 9. Then he can contribute to both sides and overloads the sides and doesn't affect so much of the balance, we found a bit of a new role for him in the last match, as a central 10, so he can go to both sides and it is more of a 4-2-3-1 than a 4-3-3 to have Harry and Jude closer together and to give them a chance to overload both sides.

Article continues below

“We are working on that. Jude in general should always be able to go through the last line and should always be able to end up in the box.

“He is a natural goalscorer and he has the hunger to be on the scoreboard. He wants to be there and have the decisive action so it makes not a huge difference if he plays as a 9 or a 10.”

Sports.title: Jurgen Klopp performs huge Man City U-turn after speaking out on guilty verdict
Sports.content:
Jurgen Klopp performs huge Man City U-turn after speaking out on guilty verdict

Jurgen Klopp was a direct rival to both Manchester City and Pep Guardiola before deciding to leave Liverpool in 2024 and he has now offered a fresh take on their guilty Premier League verdict

View 2 Images Jurgen Klopp has spoken out on the Man City charges (Image: Getty Images)

Ex-Liverpool manager Jurgen Klopp says he is not preparing to celebrate any titles in the aftermath of Manchester City’s guilty verdict. The Premier League club were found guilty of 114 of the 115 charges by an independent commission.

‌



City have maintained their innocence and will appeal the verdict on financial rule breaches. Attention, however, has now turned to a potential sanction, with relegation, a fine and points deductions all options.

‌



Others have also suggested that City should have the titles that they won during the nine-year period stripped from them and retroactively awarded to their rivals. But Klopp does not appear to be interested, having admitted his admiration for City and former boss Pep Guardiola.

‌



Speaking in a Germany press conference, he said: “Of course I've heard about that, but I haven't given it much thought. I can only wait and see. I have big respect for Pep Guardiola and City's style of football; they played fantastic football and were a top class opponent for us.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



“If any sanctions are handed out, I have nothing to do with it; I'll wait and see. I'm far from preparing for a title or anything like that. I'm absolutely fine with what we've achieved in Liverpool.

“We fought hard on the pitch. I can't say more about that because I don't know the details and I'm not interested in them.”

Liverpool finished second to Man City on three occasions in the modern era, albeit only one of those falls within the period that the club were investigated for. Klopp’s comments are somewhat of an about turn to his response from January 2025, where he vowed to celebrate should Liverpool be awarded the titles, while he has also previously joked that he would join an open top bus parade.

‌



View 2 Images Jurgen Klopp and Pep Guardiola struck up a rivalry in the Premier League (Image: Getty Images)

"We had this discussion when I left," he said. "I haven't spent a lot of time in Mallorca (where he moved after leaving Liverpool) because I am always flying around the place.

"But if it would happen, I told all the people who wanted to [come]: 'Just book a flight to Mallorca. I will buy the beer!' We'd have our own parade in my garden."

‌



Elsewhere, Klopp’s former rival Guardiola has broken his silence on the charges over recent days.

Taking to social media, the former City boss said: "I want every single Man City fan to know I am here; more than ever. I am, always have been, always will, be behind my club, my owner, my chairman, Ferran [Soriano] the players, staff, Enzo [Maresca] and you, our unique supporters. Let me be clear: we will get through this together. I love you all."

Sports.title: Jordan McCann reverses retirement just weeks after defeat to 'UK's Hardest Man'
Sports.content:
Jordan McCann reverses retirement just weeks after defeat to 'UK's Hardest Man'

The Salford rapper announced his retirement from boxing earlier this month, but has performed a major U-turn and is set to make a return to the ring next weekend

View Image Jordan McCann retired after losing to Big Stacks but is set to return next weekend

Jordan McCann has performed a retirement U-turn and will make a sensational return to the boxing ring next weekend.

‌



The Manchester rapper made his Misfits Boxing debut back in June - but would go on to lose to Ibiza Final Boss in a scrappy affair. McCann, 32, returned to action earlier this month against the 'UK's Hardest Man' - more commonly known as Big Stacks.

‌



Both men were involved in a physical altercation earlier this year and had the chance to settle their feud in the ring. And it was Stacks - real name Charlie Robert - who emerged victorious after stopping his rival in the second round. McCann was struggling to see out of his right eye and when the fight was paused in the second stanza for it to be inspected, the doctor had no option but to wave off the contest.

‌



Just days after the defeat to Stacks, McCann announced his retirement from boxing. "I really had a good time doing the Misfits. I really appreciate it and I appreciate Mams (Taylor) and stuff. But yeah, I will not be doing that again," he said in a video uploaded to social media.

But just weeks after calling it a day, Misfits announced that the Salford scrapper would be making a return to the ring next weekend and would take on Mo Deen at the Copper Box Arena in London.

The 32-year-old was quick to break his silence following the news. Commenting on a fight poster, McCann wrote: “The only person I’m getting a win from so I had 2 take it. Easy money couldn’t say no”

Sports.title: Hallgrimsson admits 'toughest days' of career after Ireland beat Israel
Sports.content:
The Republic of Ireland beat Israel 3-0 in their controversial Nations League fixture at a neutral venue in Hungary.

Players did not shake hands with each other before their meeting at the Nagyerdei Stadion in Debrecen and there was no exchange between Ireland captain Dara O'Shea and Israel's Manor Solomon.

Ireland players also appeared to bow their heads while Israel's national anthem was played out before kick-off.

Black armbands were worn by Ireland players, which Football Association of Ireland (FAI) chief executive David Courell said was a gesture to recognise "all lives lost" in the Israel-Gaza conflict.

Goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu was the only player who chose not to play after the squad voted to proceed with the match on Saturday amid calls for the game not to go ahead.

Goals from Troy Parrott, Adam Idah and Jack Moylan sealed the victory for Heimir Hallgrimsson's side.

Moylan celebrated his goal by kissing and raising his black armband before kissing his badge.

Hallgrimsson: I couldn't be more proud of the players

Republic of Ireland manager Heimir Hallgrimsson:

"It has been some of the toughest days of my coaching career, but its not about me.

"The game, the desire the players showed to make a statement on the pitch - they are football players, they wanted to show on the pitch, make that talking with their feet.

"What they did was impressive. In tough times that's when you find your leaders, there were so many players that stepped up in these tough times. The energy levels they showed was impressive.

"The performance was good given all the preparation, the lack of training, all of our meetings were about something other than football.

"I couldn't be more proud of the players.

"By playing I know we are making some people unhappy. By playing we are making others happy. Winning probably pleases everyone, but there will still be people angry that we played the game.

"I hope we can settle that slowly down and stay together as a team. I wish people in Ireland continue supporting these boys, because they certainly deserve it."

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland slip to deserved defeat in Kosovo
Sports.content:
The Republic of Ireland slipped to a 1-0 defeat away to Kosovo in their Nations League opener in Pristina.

The build-up to the League B3 encounter had been overshadowed by the controversy around upcoming fixtures against Israel, which Republic boss Heimir Hallgrimsson had admitted many of his squad members were uncomfortable about playing.

Chiedozie Ogbene had fired an early chance over before Kosovo responded to finish the first half strongly at the Fadil Vokrri Stadium.

The home side saw two shots cleared off the line and Ireland goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher then clawed away a header from Vedat Muriqi as Hallgrimsson's side got to the break on level terms.

Ireland - who are scheduled to play Israel in Hungary on Sunday and then again in a 'home' tie at another neutral venue in Serbia seven days later - dug in for the second half but were eventually undone with seven minutes left when Kosovo captain Muriqi bundled the ball in from close range.

Udinese defender James Abankwah was handed a first competitive start as part of a back five, with in-form Real Betis striker Troy Parrott the lone forward and Dara O'Shea taking the captain's armband.

Image: The Republic of Ireland have won two of their six games in 2026 so far

Ireland created what ended up being their only real clear chance in the 22nd minute. Abankwah got away down the right and ran into the Kosovo penalty area before cutting the ball back to Ogbene, who sent a curling effort over the crossbar.

Kosovo, who are in League B for the first time, went close on the half-hour mark when a cross from the left found its way through to Muriqi, whose angled shot was cleared off the line by Jayson Molumby.

Veldin Hodza then saw his 10-yard strike blocked in front of goal by O'Shea before Kelleher got up to claw away a looping header from Muriqi, which was set for the top corner.

Ireland made a positive start to the second half, with a deep cross from the right by Abankwah finding Parrott at the far post and his header was gathered by Kosovo goalkeeper Arijanet Muric.

Image: Vedat Muriqi scored the winner for Kosovo

Kosovo, though, continued to carry a threat themselves. Baton Zabergja sent a 20-yard effort just wide of the top corner, which again got the home supporters into full voice.

Muriqi forced Kelleher into another smart reaction save from an angled shot at the near post before Kosovo eventually made the breakthrough in the 83rd minute.

Ermal Krasniqi's shot was deflected onto the crossbar and Muriqi reacted quickest in a crowded six-yard box to nod the ball over the line.

Kosovo should have got a second late on when substitute Krasniqi dragged his shot wide after being set up by Muriqi following a break onto a long ball.

Ireland pay price for 'off day'

Ireland manager Heimir Hallgrimsson told RTE:

"[Kosovo are] a good team, momentum with them, crowd with them, and to be honest they deserve the win.

"There was nothing that we didn't know about how they would play, where their threats would be, but [it was] an off day for a lot of our players and [it is] a tough place to come to if you have an off day, so a deserved win for Kosovo."

Hallgrimsson added: "We were the team that needed to defend today and didn't connect in possession or passes, not as sharp as we have done.

"We have to quickly find out the reason that we had an off day. We can all do better than we did today.

"It is a two-day turnaround for the next one, so we better be quick…and do better than this versus Israel. They are probably in the same position as us [having lost to Austria]."

Asked if the controversy from playing the fixtures against Israel had impacted on his team's performance against Kosovo, Hallgrimsson said: "I couldn't say now. It is difficult to measure that one."

He added: "This is the situation, we have to cope with it. And like I said before the game, this camp is a test of character.

"We need to do better in that area than we did here today. We knew that we needed to win the duels, win the one-vs-ones, but sadly they had the upper hand on all the basics."

What it means and next fixtures

Sports.title: Why have the Republic of Ireland's two games against Israel become so controversial?
Sports.content:
The Republic of Ireland will face Israel in a men’s football fixture for the first time since 2005 in this international break, but there have been calls for the two UEFA Nations League games not to be played at all.

Both meetings - the first played in Debrecen, Hungary on Sunday and the second scheduled for the Serbian town of Backa Topola on October 4 - have been overshadowed by politics, with the Football Association of Ireland (FAI) urged to boycott the internationals amid ongoing conflict in the Israel-Gaza War.

Uncertainty over the games going ahead might have subsided, but the tensions between the two nations have not.

Heimir Hallgrimsson, the Republic of Ireland head coach, has been accused of "stupidity and hypocrisy" by the Israel Football Association after last week suggesting his team would be "playing against genocide" when facing Israel, while his players are not ruling out their own protests ahead of the games.

The Athletic examines the key issues ahead of the first meeting this weekend.

Why have these games caused controversy?

This has been a contentious issue rolling down the tracks ever since the 2026-27 Nations League draw was made in February. Group B3 saw the Republic of Ireland pitted against Kosovo, their opening opponents this evening, and Austria, but it was the prospect of facing Israel which created immediate unease.

The Football Association of Ireland (FAI) had overwhelmingly approved a motion that called on UEFA to ban Israel from its competitions just four months earlier due to violations of the governing body's statutes, including "the organisation of clubs in illegal settlements in the occupied West Bank without the consent of the Palestinian Football Association".

The Nations League draw duly reignited the row. Irish politicians, including the FAI member Joanna Byrne, were quick to call for a boycott of the Israel games in the following days and protests ensued when Qatar visited Dublin's Aviva Stadium for a friendly in May. Tennis balls featuring the Palestine flag were thrown on the pitch by supporters, twice causing brief interruptions.

Image: Tennis balls with a Palestinian flag on were thrown onto the pitch in Dublin during protests in May 2026

The FAI had already confirmed its plans to go ahead with the Israel games by then, and that decision was formally approved at an EGM in July.

That saw only 32 votes in favour of a boycott, with 75 members voting for the games to be played. The FAI had argued that boycotting games would cause "significant and lasting harm to Irish football" due to the likely disciplinary sanctions from UEFA.

A measure of the opposition to the Republic of Ireland facing Israel also came with the acceptance that the "home" fixture would not be played in Dublin. The FAI cited "operational challenges (that) could impact the delivery of the game on home soil" and the decision was eventually made in late June, with the support of UEFA, to move the game to Backa Topola, a small town in northern Serbia, on Sunday week.

No tickets for the game will be made available to Ireland fans.

The FAI has subsequently revealed that a request to see the two nations kept apart in future competition draws has been rejected by UEFA.

"The answer I got was very clear," FAI chief executive David Courell told reporters on September 18. "That would not be possible because Ireland and Israel have never been in direct conflict."

What is the political backdrop?

The Republic of Ireland has consistently outlined its backing for the Palestinian people since the conflict with Israel began almost three years ago, joining Norway and Spain when officially recognising a Palestinian state in 2024. Taoiseach Micheal Martin has also made his stance clear, accusing Israel of committing "genocide" last year in comments reported by the Irish Mirror.

The conflict in Gaza began after Israel responded to attacks by Hamas militants on October 7, 2023, which saw around 1,200 people, mostly civilians, killed in Israel and 250 taken hostage. The war has subsequently seen 73,000 people killed, according to figures from the Gaza Health Ministry and used by the UN.

Strained relations between the Republic of Ireland and Israel have continued this year. Two Israeli government ministers were the subject of travel bans in June, while foreign minister Helen McEntee also confirmed Ireland's intent to limit goods trading with settlements in the Israeli-occupied West Bank this summer.

Image: Taoiseach Micheal Martin

A meeting between the Republic of Ireland and Israel on a football field this weekend has subsequently taken on enormous significance against such a backdrop.

There are similarities in Ireland's political stance with those of Norway, who faced similar calls for a boycott when Israel travelled to Oslo last October. The Norwegian Football Federation (NFF) had aligned itself with its government and said in a statement leading up to Israel's visit that the "tragic humanitarian suffering in Gaza" had made the fixture challenging.

That World Cup qualifier, won 5-0 by Norway, saw thousands take part in a protest march to the stadium.

Who has opposed the games taking place?

Moving a home game 1,500 miles away has not stopped the objections building ahead of the two teams meeting on Sunday. More than 160 Irish sportspeople signed an open letter asking their national team to boycott the Israel games under the banner of the Irish Sport for Palestine Group, who have also run the "Stop the Game" campaign that protested outside of the Irish team hotel in Dublin on Monday.

"This is a significant moment and with this moment you have an opportunity to do the right thing," the letter said.

Kevin Kilbane, the former Republic of Ireland international who holds 110 caps, has also been unequivocal in his views. "The Republic of Ireland should not be playing Israel… not while Israeli forces are committing genocide," he wrote in a column for the Irish Times.">he wrote in a column for the Irish Times.

Amnesty International also issued a fresh statement on Tuesday that said UEFA risked letting football "rubber-stamp apartheid" by allowing Israel's continued participation in its club and international competitions. A spokesperson for the Israeli FA responded to that by saying: "Their obsession with the idea of Israel as a state is incurable, as is their need of attention."

The Irish media, meanwhile, has faced its own dilemmas in the coverage of the Israel games. RTE, the public broadcaster behind Ireland's boycott of the Eurovision Song Contest in the last two years due to Israel's continued involvement, has stripped back its coverage. Contractual obligations will be met, RTE confirmed in a statement, but there would be no studio coverage or commentators sent to either fixture.

Image: Kevin Kilbane, former Ireland international, has spoken out

What have the key stakeholders said ahead of this weekend?

Relations between the two nations have grown increasingly hostile in the last week. Hallgrimsson appeared in front of the media to announce his squad for the upcoming friendlies and made pointed remarks when asked how his players would focus on football.

"We're not playing with genocide, we're playing against genocide," the former Iceland head coach told reporters. "We're playing against Israel, we're not playing with Israel."

The reaction to those words, in a social media post from the Israel FA account, raised temperatures further still. "We have contributed to the world and humanity in countless fields, earning an impressive number of Nobel Prizes along the way," it read. "Unfortunately, we have not yet found a cure for stupidity, ignorance and hypocrisy displayed by @IrelandFootball team coach. We're not playing with ignorance, hypocrisy and stupidity, we're playing against the coach who embodies them."

Martin, who was among the world leaders attending the UN General Assembly in New York, was then drawn back into debate on Tuesday. "I think those are unacceptable remarks. They should be withdrawn. Israel can't keep denying what the world knows and what the world understands."

The FAI has not addressed Hallgrimsson's comments publicly, but the Republic of Ireland's head coach said on Wednesday that he had been "grateful for the support" he had received.

"Maybe from a leadership point of view, it was not clever from me to take the attention (away) like this. It's a tricky time for us," Hallgrimsson said in his pre-match press conference ahead of facing Kosovo.

The same extends to his players, too. Dara O'Shea, the Ipswich Town defender, said, according to the BBC, that he and the rest of the players would come together on Friday to "openly discuss" the prospect of a protest ahead of the first Israel game in Debrecen on Sunday.

Image: Dara O’Shea, left, and head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson during Wednesday’s press conference

Why are the games being played in Hungary and Serbia?

Hungary has acted as an adopted home for Israel since the start of the conflict. They first played there in November 2023, when resuming their attempts to qualify for Euro 2024 when hosting Switzerland at the Pancho Arena in Felcsut, a small village 26 miles west of Budapest.

Victor Orban, who lost his position as Hungary's prime minister this year, had been a long-standing ally of Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu and claimed Hungary to be the "safest country in Europe" for Jews.

The World Cup 2026 qualifiers against Estonia, Norway and Italy were all held in Debrecen, which has also previously hosted European games for Israeli sides Maccabi Haifa and Maccabi Tel Aviv.

The Republic of Ireland's choice of Backa Topola, Serbia, is less clear. Dublin ceased to become an option, even behind closed doors, as the opposition to Israel visiting became clear, which left limited options for relocation.

It needed to be a nation sympathetic to Israel to avoid further protests and Serbia, neighbouring Hungary to the south, has forged strong diplomatic relations. According to the Associated Press, Serbia's president Aleksandar Vucic inaugurated an assembly factory for Israel-made drones last week, with plans for three more production sites.

A switch to Serbia was reliant on UEFA approval and it will be Backa Topola's home of the TSC Arena where this story ends on October 4.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."

Collins: Ireland must build on World Cup near miss

Ireland captain Nathan Collins is confident his side have laid the foundations to qualify for future tournaments having seen hopes of reaching this summer's World Cup finals come to an end.

Collins and his team-mates were agonisingly close to the play-off final when they led the Czech Republic 2-1 in Prague on Thursday evening with just four minutes of normal time remaining.

Image: A dejected Nathan Collins and head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson

However, Czech skipper Ladislav Krejci's late equaliser took the tie to extra-time and ultimately to penalties, where the hosts prevailed 4-3 to extend Ireland's wait for a first return to the big stage since 2002.

Asked about their progression to the play-offs, which was secured by back-to-back wins over Armenia, Portugal and Hungary, Brentford defender Collins said: "I'm not seeing many positives right now because we're in the gutter.

"But what we've created, the environment created with the fans and country, has been special. That's something we need to keep growing, to get even better at.

"That can help us get better on the pitch. We can push that and get fans to more tournaments."

Ireland had hoped to return to the Aviva Stadium on Tuesday for a showdown with either Denmark or North Macedonia for a place in the finals, but the Czechs will now host the Danes, who were 4-0 winners in Copenhagen.

Instead, Heimir Hallgrimsson's side face a friendly against the Macedonians.

Collins said: "The motivation has to be the same. We've to win to keep improving as a team and country. Any game we play at home is a big game."

Sports.title: Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua press conference LIVE: Heavyweight rivals trade insults and clash over Eddie Hearn
Sports.content:
Right, that's it for today.

The first presser is over and now we have two months to wait until we see both Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua go face-to-face again.

Let's hope the next time they face off and have words, it's a bit more fiery and feisty. That was all too nice for me.

Anyway, thanks for joining us for this live coverage and I will see you all very soon.

Goodnight.

Sports.title: Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua's £150m mega-fight is back ON: Heavyweight rivals set to meet in London face off TOMORROW after Gypsy King claimed rival 'tried to pull out' amid Eddie Hearn's feud with Dana White
Sports.content:
It's on. At last. Finally. Confirmed by the almighty Turki.

Reconfirmed by the late, late word sent out that the face to face stare down between our two heavyweight titans will definitely take place at a press conference launch this Wednesday.

The fight that almost got away. AJ versus the Gypsy King. So close to being another of boxing's lost jewels that we almost gave up hope.

May the lords of the rings be praised.

Whether or not Dana White, the American interloper from UFC cage fighting who is demanding a share of the action, is present despite the protestations of Joshua's promoter Eddie Hearn, who won the battle for this fight to take place if not at Wembley but not as far, far west of London as New York.

Anthony Joshua v Tyson Fury has been rescued for the British fight fans, by Cardiff. Although like the 70-odd thousand in the Principality Stadium the TV majority will have to stay awake into the wee small hours on the Friday night of December 11.

Anthony Joshua and Tyson Fury will face each other down at a press conference on Wednesday

Fury and Joshua's fight is due to take place on December 11 in Cardiff with the showdown set to begin at 2am so Netflix subscribers can stream it at peak time in America

Fury against Joshua was almost the fight that got away, with the heavyweights now set to sort out differences that should have been settled a decade ago

First bell about 2am so that the tens of millions of Netflix subscribers can stream at peak time in America.

Assuming they buy into this as being a mega fight for all time. Or are satisfied that it is a spectacle unto itself.

Maybe a world heavyweight title adding spice to the occasion. Maybe not. Maybe just two good old Brits sorting differences that should have been settled a decade ago.

And why not? Fury and Joshua may be past their prime but they are not yet the walking dead.

They have enough fight left in their late 30s to put on a show.

And a future to fight for. For the winner there can be challenges to meet from the new generation of champions and a few million dollars more to add to the 75 million each will receive as an early Christmas present.

Always assuming no more spanners are thrown into these on-off-on works.

Good luck to both. Even more so to the Welsh constabulary who will have to deal with all those fans spilling out into darkened streets on what will already be a typically wild Friday night in Cardiff.

Sports.title: For Scottish boxing, the cupboard is bare. All that remains are memories of better times
Sports.content:
For Scottish boxing, the cupboard is bare. All that remains are memories of better times

Given the endless nonsense that continues to surround the Tyson Fury-Anthony Joshua fight, it’s no surprise that it has dominated all the recent headlines in boxing.

Will they? Won’t they? Does anyone even really care any more? Is it happening in the UK? America? Saudi Arabia? Maybe on the moon? For a gazillion dollars?

It felt like a degree of certainty had been reached last week with the announcement that the fight will go ahead at the Principality Stadium in Cardiff in December.

That was until Dana White, the UFC supremo and one of the fight’s chief promoters, said only a few days ago that he ‘doesn’t know’ if it will go ahead.

Perhaps we will get a clearer picture tomorrow afternoon, with Fury and Joshua set to face-off at a media conference in London.

Either way, this tiresome circus act involving two fighters long past their prime continues to be pretty much the only thing anyone is speaking about in boxing right now.

Josh Taylor is dominated by Jack Catterall in Leeds as his ring supremacy is left in ruins

Nathaniel Collins had been Scotland's biggest hope until he suffered two successive defeats

Taylor's rise to the top of the fight game was an incredible achievement that will long be lauded

It perhaps escaped your attention, then, that Scotland’s Nathaniel Collins was back in the ring last weekend. Quite an important fight it was, too.

Taking on European featherweight champion Liam Davies in Birmingham, this was supposed to be Collins’ comeback fight after he lost to Spain’s Cristobal Llorente in Glasgow in April in their world title eliminator.

It did not go well. Collins was floored in the first round and never really recovered, before his trainer put a stop to it all and said enough was enough at the end of the seventh round.

There was a sadness to it all. Not only that Collins had suffered a second successive defeat, but also in terms of the wider implications for himself and for Scottish boxing as a whole.

The defeat to Llorente at The Hydro had been the first loss of Collins’ career. It had been a tough night, albeit not disastrous. There was a chance to bounce back and come again.

But, in terms of challenging at world level, he now looks further away than ever. The same would surely apply to Scottish boxing as a whole after this latest blow.

Not so long ago, Scottish boxing felt like it had a pulse. Josh Taylor climbed the mountain and was, in his pomp, one of the best pound-for-pound fighters on the planet.

The Tartan Tornado put together one of the greatest runs by any British fighter in history to become our first undisputed world champion in the four-belt era. Achieving that in just 18 fights was truly phenomenal.

When Taylor’s career then fizzled out due to a combination of burn-out, inactivity and promotional mismanagement, it had been hoped that Collins would be the next cab off the rank.

The late Ken Buchanan won multiple titles at lightweight and fought between 1965 and 1982

The Nightmare, as he’s known, was supposed to be the fighter who kept the lights on and continued to fly the flag in the post-Taylor era.

That’s not to say he was ever going to be quite as good as Taylor. That always looked unrealistic. But there was genuine hope that Collins could at least be a contender for a world title.

The brutal yet stylish manner in which he dismantled fellow Scot Lee McGregor at The Hydro in May 2025 gave the look of a fighter with all the credentials to go on and box at world level.

But the defeat to Davies in Birmingham last weekend has surely ended that conversation. In the post-Taylor era, the cupboard is depressingly bare for Scottish boxing. Completely and utterly empty.

No one is selling out arenas in Scotland. No one is forcing their way on to Sky Sports and the likes. No one is even close to holding box-office appeal or appearing on pay-per-views.

The amateur and club scene are still doing their bit. The numbers are OK, even if a lot of people use boxing clubs as fitness classes these days rather than having any desire to actually enter a ring.

But when you speak to people involved with boxing clubs across Scotland, the majority of them all share a similar concern.

Plainly, that we have no one even remotely close to following in Taylor’s footsteps and fighting at the top level of the sport. The outlook is bleak.

Listen, Scotland is a relatively small country. We do not have an endless pool of talent. Boxing is not a mainstream sport like football or rugby.

The two successive defeats for Collins have signaled a barren period for Scottish boxing

Kids learn to play football in various different ways; at school, at coaching sessions, or with a club. Maybe even down the local park or on the streets in some very rare and old-fashioned instances.

Rugby is a non-negotiable for those in private education. Even golf now has far more reach and appeal with the younger generation than boxing.

With the awareness around long-term brain damage now greater than ever, you can hardly blame any parent if they aren’t overly enthused by the idea of their kids being involved in a sport where they get punched in the head.

When a generational talent like Taylor comes along and then leaves, the gap is enormous. There is no conveyor belt of world-class operators waiting in the wings.

Sadly, it also now appears that Scotland can’t even offer up any fighters in the bracket just below world level either.

Collins has already come through a serious health scare – a life-threatening twisted bowel caused by infant scar tissue – that put much more than just his boxing career at risk. He has shown heart. No one questions that. He gave it a good go.

But his latest defeat is emblematic of the wider malaise that continues to be so prevalent across Scottish boxing as a whole.

There have been lean times in the past. After Ken Buchanan and Jim Watt, there were quiet periods. After Scott Harrison’s turbulent reign at featherweight the scene thinned out again until Ricky Burns and then Taylor arrived.

Cycles exist. The problem now is that the cycle feels stuck in the downward phase with no obvious sign of it moving back up again.

Where is the next boxing superstar in Scotland? It is beginning to feel like the sport is dying a death. That is the uncomfortable truth.

When Collins fought Llorente at The Hydro in April, it wasn’t even close to being a sell-out. The whole top tier of the arena was closed. Make of that what you will.

And that was a world title eliminator involving the guy who was supposed to be our next big hope. Taylor himself has acknowledged the lack of young fighters breaking through.

The Tornado’s retirement left a void. Collins’ latest defeat has made it wider and deeper. The Hydro still stands ready for big nights, but it’s hard to see a major promoter going back there any time soon.

The Scottish public still loves a fighter who will dig in and go to war. But the fighters of genuine world-class pedigree are simply not here at present.

These are the lean years. The barren stretch. And that should worry anyone who cares about the sport north of the border.

The cupboard is bare. The stars have gone. Until someone steps forward and proves otherwise, Scottish boxing is living on memories of Taylor and on nostalgia about some of the other great names of the past.

Sports.title: Tyson Fury enrolls in drug testing programme after Anthony Joshua threatened to boycott London press conference ahead of £150m Cardiff bout
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury enrolls in drug testing programme after Anthony Joshua threatened to boycott London press conference ahead of £150m Cardiff bout

Tyson Fury has now enrolled in the Voluntary Anti-Doping Association (VADA)'s testing programme ahead of his blockbuster showdown with Anthony Joshua, his camp has confirmed.

The development comes just 24 hours after Joshua threatened to boycott Wednesday's first press conference in London unless Fury could prove he had entered the VADA testing pool.

Joshua had already enrolled, while Fury's camp maintained that the terms of their agreement gave him longer to do so.

But with the first face-to-face meeting between the two heavyweights this Wednesday, Fury has now completed his enrolment and provided his whereabouts to VADA.

Fury's manager, Spencer Brown, told Playbook Boxing: 'We are enrolled in VADA. We are enrolled in VADA. Just to confirm that.'

Asked about the timing of Fury's enrolment, they added: 'He did it a bit earlier than when the fight was announced. In our contract, we had more time, but you know, it doesn't matter. We've done it. We've done everything we've been asked to do. Everything.'

Tyson Fury has agreed to join a drug testing programme after Anthony Joshua threatened to boycott their press conference

The Gypsy King's manager also explained that enrolment and testing are separate stages of the VADA process.

Asked whether Fury had already been tested, they said: 'No, you have to enrol first, don't you? That part of it's all been done, then the testing comes second.'

Brown stressed that the nature of VADA's programme means fighters are not given advance warning of when testers will arrive.

'You could be tested in a week, you could be sitting there on your toilet and they knock on the door,' he said. 'That's the way they work. They don't tell you a time. They don't say we're coming round tomorrow. That's the way. That's why it works.'

The dispute had threatened to become an unwanted subplot to a fight more than a decade in the making.

Joshua's camp had raised concerns after it emerged that the two fighters had different timelines under their respective contractual arrangements, with promoter Eddie Hearn subsequently making clear that he expected Fury to enter the programme.

There is now another significant issue to resolve before December 11: exactly when the fight will take place.

The heavyweight blockbuster will be staged at Cardiff's Principality Stadium and streamed globally by Netflix, with organisers targeting the US primetime market. The main event is expected to take place in the early hours of Saturday morning in Britain, with a ring walk potentially as late as 2am.

Fury and Joshua's fight is due to take place on Friday December 11. The pair are set to meet for a press conference on September 30

Brown has now revealed that the precise timing is still being negotiated and made clear that he does not want the fight to start at 2am.

'I think 2am is far too late,' he said.

'I think that the general public in England will want to watch it in the pubs, the clubs, you know, round each other's houses. There'll be a party atmosphere, and I just think it needs to be earlier. Simple as that.'

Brown added: 'It's all in negotiation at the moment, but it shouldn't be at 2 o'clock in the morning. I certainly wouldn't like to sit there at 2 o'clock in the morning, would you?'

And Brown also questioned the experience for the thousands of fans expected to attend in Cardiff.

'I think 99 per cent of the people will probably tell you that if you're in the stadium, you don't want to be sitting in the stadium till 2 o'clock in the morning, freezing your nuts off.'

The late start has been driven by the fact Netflix is looking to maximise its US audience, while Cardiff's Principality Stadium was selected after the proposed venues in London could not accommodate the required late finish.

The venue can accommodate the late finish, but the event's licensing arrangements have also required negotiation because of the proposed early-hours schedule.

Fury and Joshua are due to meet for the first time in public since their long-awaited fight was officially confirmed at Wednesday's press conference in London.

The bout, which will be contested at Cardiff's Principality Stadium on December 11, is the culmination of years of failed negotiations between the former world champions.

Both men have won their respective comeback fights this year, clearing the way for the long-awaited all-British heavyweight showdown.

Now, with Fury's VADA enrolment confirmed, attention can turn back to the build-up and whether organisers can find a start time that works for both the global Netflix audience and the British fans inside and outside the stadium.

Sports.title: Dana White admits he 'doesn't know' if Tyson Fury's fight with Anthony Joshua will go ahead after Gypsy King claimed rival wants to pull OUT of the £150m bout amid Eddie Hearn's feud with promoter
Sports.content:
Dana White admits he 'doesn't know' if Tyson Fury's fight with Anthony Joshua will go ahead after Gypsy King claimed rival wants to pull OUT of the £150m bout amid Eddie Hearn's feud with promoter

Dana White has cast doubt over Tyson Fury's heavyweight blockbuster against Anthony Joshua, admitting that he has 'no idea' whether the £150million showdown will go ahead on December 11.

The battle between British boxing's biggest names was plunged into jeopardy over the weekend, with Fury claiming his arch rival 'wants to pull out' of the fight amid a dispute between White and Joshua's promoter Eddie Hearn.

Fury's claim made for a dramatic escalation, with the pair announcing their Cardiff bout just over 24 hours earlier.

White, who runs Zuffa Boxing alongside Saudi Arabia's boxing supremo Turki Al-Sheikh, has been billed as the main promoter for the heavyweight showdown and had fought for the contest to take place in New York City.

Hearn, who successfully wrestled the fight back to Cardiff, has claimed that the contract Joshua signed stipulates that White cannot be involved in the contest and threatened crunch talks with broadcaster Netflix over White's attendance at Fury and Joshua's press conference on Wednesday in London.

That warning appears to have thrown the event into chaos, with Fury claiming Hearn's 'ego' is presenting a major stumbling block in the long-awaited bout taking place.

Dana White has admitted he has 'no idea' if Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua will go ahead

Tyson Fury announced on Saturday that Joshua 'wants to pull out' of the December 11 contest

White, whose involvement has been criticised by sections of the British boxing public, was grilled by the media in a cagey press conference on Saturday night, where he labelled the bout a 's***show' while conceding he has 'no idea' if the contest will take place.

'I don't know. The guy who is supposed to be helping the fight has been hurting the fight the entire time. He hasn't done the fight any favours. I don't know anybody who is more full of s*** than Eddie Hearn.'

When asked whether he would step aside to allow the fight to go ahead, White said: 'That's not up to me. I'm involved in the f***ing fight.

'If Eddie Hearn really cared about this f***ing fight — first of all the fight would've happened a f***ing long time ago, one. Number two, he could finance the thing himself.

'Listen, this whole thing's a s***show right now. We'll all know a lot more in the next three, four days, see how this thing plays out.'

White's comments follow Fury's expletive-laden Instagram video, in which he labelled Joshua and Hearn 'cowards'.

He said: 'Breaking News: Anthony Joshua and Eddie Hearn are trying to pull out of this fight they are saying he is not going to fight now.

'They're little s*** house cowards, mainly to do with Eddie Hearn's ego, he's making up a million different things and threatening that "we're not going to fight" you little coward.

Fury and Joshua have been on a collision course for 15 years but a fight has never transpired

Fury and Joshua's fight was due to take place on Friday December 11. The pair are set to meet for a press conference on September 30

'AJ pull your finger out you white flag, yellow-bellied coward. You know now we're coming home, now I'm coming home the Gypsy King is coming back to the United Kingdom to thrash you in front of all my fans in Wales.'

Fury went on to call Joshua a 'body-building sausage'.

He also claimed that boxing supremo Turki Al-Sheikh is now looking to find a new person to fight Fury at 'the drop of a hat'.

Fury continued: 'So I hope [Hearn and Joshua] are happy you little cowardly b*******, I've never seen anything like [Hearn and Joshua] you pure s*** houses and this is mainly to do with Eddie Hearn's ego. What a little p****.'

The 38-year-old then posted a mocked up poster of himself and light heavyweight champion David Benavidez, hinting that the 29-year-old American could replace AJ in the Cardiff contest.

It is understood that both men are set to pocket around £75million for arguably the biggest bout to be staged on British soil, if it goes ahead.
