World.title: Dulwich gallery chief: Konrad Mägi show exceeded our expectations
World.content:
An exhibition in London of Estonian artist Konrad Mägi's work exceeded all expectations, the gallery's director said.

The work by Mägi, famed for both hits landscapes and portraits, was on display at the Dulwich Picture Gallery in South London and drew more than 37,000 visitors, director

Jennifer Scott said while on a visit to Mägi's home country.

The exhibition ran from the end of March to mid-July.

"It was a hit, and we knew, we could tell, that the art of Kondrad Mägi would work well beautifully in London, but it exceeded even our high expectations – it was the most loved exhibition. We had almost 100 percent of the feedback saying that the visitors loved this exhibition, and the only criticism was they want more – they want more Mägi, it was so wonderful," gallery director Jennifer Scott told "Ringvaade".

Rembrandts and Rubens hang on the Dulwich's 200-year-old walls, but the gallery also dedicates itself to showcasing artists who are lesser known in the U.K., Mägi among them.

Dulwich gallery patrons, who Scott said included business-people, pensioners and collectors alike, contribute around £10,000 a year to the museum's work, and many of them have now visited Estonia off the back of the Mägi exhibition's reception.

The Konrad Mägi exhibition in Dulwich, London. Source: ERR

As well as the national art museum, Kumu, in Tallinn, the visitors went to Tartu and to Saaremaa. Scott had just braved the autumnal weather on Saaremaa, which includes the Vilsandi lighthouse, the focal point of several Mägi paintings. "I loved it, we all all loved it, because also it's a reason to come back – this is our taster tour with the patrons, and all of us are saying we will come back, so we will come back in the summer and see Saaremaa," she enthused.

"The last room, where we saw big, wonderful contemporary art paintings displayed really innovatively – so I thought the way you're displaying the art, as well as the art itself, is actually really interesting, from a museum point of view. I loved it, the visit was great," added Dame Janet Vitmayer, one of the patrons and British Museum director who also visited Estonia.

Scott noted that Kumu lingered in the visitors' memories, thanks to its architecture and interior design, the warm reception and of course the art collection itself. She highlighted Kumu's famous scultpure bust room as another attraction.

Art collector Enn Kunila hopes the Mägi exhibition shown in London will travel elsewhere in the future too.

"We have had it before that each exhibition has led to the next. I think the exhibition in London should be able to do that too," Kunila said.

The original "Ringvaade" segment can be viewed by clicking on the video player below.

Konrad Mägi (1878–1925) was one of Estonia's first modernist painters, working for only 16 years but producing around 400 paintings in that relatively short time. His work has been on display across Europe in recent years, including in Rome and Paris. The Dulwich exhibition was the first time his art had been shown in the U.K.

Not everyone was a fan of the Dulwich exhibition, however: The Guardian's Jonathan Jones described them as "bland, blobby paintings" and "expressionism without expression," handing the exhibition a one-star review.

World.title: Kodumaa Kapital savings and loan association declared bankrupt by court
World.content:
The Harju District Court declared the bankruptcy of the Kodumaa Kapital savings and loan association in mid‑September.

Kodumaa Kapital stopped paying out money to depositors at the start of this year, saying the halt was caused by changes to the Savings and Loan Associations Act, Ärileht reported.

In February, a letter sent to depositors offered them the chance to exchange their claims for units in the Kodumaa Fund. The trust fund was presented as a solution that would protect depositors' interests and emphasized growing members' money and avoiding shutting down operations.

The letter to depositors said the Kodumaa group's loan portfolio — Kodumaa Kapital and Kodumaa Laenud — would become the trust fund's assets.

Depositors went to court, suspecting asset transfers, because the association moved its main asset — a €2 million loan portfolio — into the new Kodumaa Fund through a subsidiary.

Kodumaa Kapital's board currently includes Kiur Lootus and Pille Lõugas. Reform Party politician Tõnis Kõiv left the board in the summer of 2025. He had led the association since 2021 but reportedly continues as an adviser.

Creditors must notify the bankruptcy trustee of all claims that arose before the bankruptcy declaration no later than November 15. Claims submitted late but recognized will be satisfied in the final order.

World.title: Rescue chief: Estonia short of more than 100 firefighters as pay lags
World.content:
Estonia's rescue service needs around 100 more personnel, its deputy director has said, warning pay remains too low and the shortfall threatens response capacity.

Martin Lambing, the Rescue Board's (Päästeamet) deputy director, said while the service has 34 unfilled positions officially, the real need is over 100

This would allow fully staffing four-person rescue and three-person ordnance disposal teams, he went on.

'Working at the current understaffed levels means crews at certain moments operate with as much as double a standard workload, and with it double the risk, a risk which can also be passed on to the public.

While the rescue service's wage fund received a small increase for next year, this is not a fair rise, Lambing went on.

Under the freshly announced 2027 state budget, firefighters' pay will rise €48 per month to €1,654.

"The pay rise — as far as the cost-of-living component goes — the fact that firefighters got a raise is welcome. But where the dissatisfaction comes in is purely related to the fact that when we look at firefighters' current and future pay and compare it to the average wage and how the average wage is moving, the gap is large and that shortfall keeps growing," Lambing said.

Martin Lambing. Source: ERR

According to Lambing, a fair level for firefighters would be 1.2 times the national average. "That takes into account the risk of the work, the responsibility and the movement towards it. Today this pay and this pay rise certainly do not reduce that gap," he said.

Lambing added firefighters' work and civil protection as a whole are part of national defense, and that if firefighters were to leave their posts it would create a security risk.

"The risk arises simply because these people are highly qualified. They are skilled workers who know how to do this job, and such employees are not easy to find," Lambing said. "When a decision is reached and a person leaves, it is not the case that they go one day and come back the next. And for the rescue system that is a great loss, because they have been through very complex long-term training and if they have also been on the job for years, they are genuinely very competent people."

At the same time, Lambing conceded politicians have not had an easy task finding solutions.

"The Rescue Board, the Ministry of the Interior and also the union — we are actually standing for one goal: to move towards 1.2 times the Estonian average wage. Finding solutions for permanent funding for civil protection and valuing voluntary rescue in the same way — that is a common goal and joint efforts are being made towards it," he went on.

Lambing credited Interior Minister Igor Taro (Eesti 200), noting he has fought for firefighters' pay and for crisis preparedness.

Lambing added there are currently 1,700 professional firefighters, augmented by over 3,000 volunteers. Officially while there are 34 unfilled positions, including firefighters and crew leaders with higher-level qualifications to lead complex rescue events, taking a broader context including national defense needs into account, the shortfall is more than 100 personnel, Lambing concluded.

World.title: Ronaldo leaves Portugal training camp after coach says he is dropped
World.content:
Copenhagen – Portugal captain Cristiano Ronaldo announced on Wednesday that he had left the team’s training camp in Denmark after coach Jorge Jesus told reporters that the striker would be dropped for their next match.

Ronaldo had been due to train with his team-mates at the Parken stadium in Copenhagen on Wednesday but left abruptly after Jesus’s press conference.

The veteran coach had said that Ronaldo, who spent the entire match on the bench against Norway on Sunday, would not start Thursday’s Nations League clash away to Denmark either.

“Following the national team coach’s press conference, and after having a conversation with the Portuguese Football Federation president, I decided to leave the national team’s training camp,” Ronaldo wrote on Instagram.

“In due course, I will tell the truth to all the Portuguese people about my reasons for leaving the national team, to which I have always been dedicated.

“Now is time to wish good luck to Portugal and to all my team-mates, without exception.”

Jesus had insisted earlier that there was no rift between him and Ronaldo, although the 72-year-old did acknowledge that his captain had been disappointed to remain on the bench in the side’s Nations League win over Norway.

– ‘No incident’ –

Following the 2-1 victory in Oslo, Ronaldo went straight to the changing rooms without joining his team-mates in acknowledging the Portuguese supporters in the stands.

“There was no incident whatsoever,” Jesus told reporters.

“Any player –- and I was a player myself… when you spend 20 or 30 minutes warming up and then don’t get on… no one is happy about that,” Jesus said on Wednesday.

The Portuguese coach added that he had told Ronaldo before the match that he would not be in the starting line-up, but that he might bring him on towards the end of the game.

“Afterwards, as coach, I decided not to bring him on. It’s nothing to make a fuss about,” Jesus insisted.

The former Benfica boss also explained that Ronaldo had not refused to train on Tuesday, as some Portuguese media outlets had suggested, but that he had had to do individual exercises for physical “mobility” and “strengthening”.

Jesus had said that the five-time Ballon d’Or winner would train as normal on Wednesday, however, despite arriving at the stadium in the team bus, Ronaldo did not join his team-mates on the pitch in Copenhagen.

Portuguese media shared a video of him leaving the Parken stadium alongside two members of the backroom staff just after Jesus’s press conference.

They also said that Ronaldo’s private jet was heading to Copenhagen.

Just before Ronaldo’s social media post, the Portuguese federation had released a brief statement merely confirming that the former Real Madrid, Manchester United and Juventus player had not trained.

Jesus had said earlier that for the Denmark match he again intended to start AC Milan striker Goncalo Ramos, who scored the winner against the Norwegians.

“If everything goes according to plan, it will be Goncalo who plays,” he said, before adding regarding Ronaldo: “If I need him, he’ll come on. If I don’t need him, he won’t.”

At 41, Ronaldo announced this summer that this season would “probably (be) my last year in football”.

He is Portugal’s leading goalscorer and most capped player, with 146 goals in 234 appearances.

World.title: Kataib Hezbollah suspends operations as US forces leave Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s Iran-aligned Kataib Hezbollah declared the cessation of military activities on Wednesday, the first day of the country’s post-coalition period.

The declaration came after US Central Command concluded the evacuation of American personnel and equipment from Erbil Air Base, thereby concluding the US-led Operation Inherent Resolve operation in Iraq.

Kataib Hezbollah has long opposed the presence of American forces in Iraq and has been one of the most vocal armed groups calling for their removal.

The group and other Iran-aligned militias have previously launched or claimed assaults on US soldiers and military facilities.

The suspension comes at a critical time for Baghdad, as the evacuation of US soldiers eliminates one of the primary grounds stated by armed groups for conducting military operations outside of Iraqi official institutions.

The United States’ withdrawal puts an end to the coalition campaign, which started in 2014 after ISIS conquered Mosul and huge parts of northern and western Iraq.

American soldiers had already invaded Iraq in 2003, primarily withdrawing in 2011, and returning three years later at Baghdad’s request to assist in the battle against ISIS.

The coalition’s departure has shifted focus to the future of Iraq’s armed groups, as well as Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi’s attempts to put armaments and military decision-making under state control.

The Iraqi government said on Wednesday that talks with armed groups on integration into state structures were ongoing, as Baghdad took full responsibility for the country’s security.

The problem is expected to be one of the most crucial challenges for Al-Zaidi after the US pullout.

Several armed groups continue to wield substantial military and political power while nominally working inside or alongside Iraq’s governmental security apparatus.

Kataib Hezbollah, which developed during the 2003 US-led invasion, grew to be one of Iraq’s most formidable Iran-aligned militias, eventually fighting ISIS as part of a larger mobilization of Iraqi armed groups.

The group’s cessation of activities comes as Iraq starts a new security phase after more than two decades of US military engagement.

The next problem for Baghdad will be to determine whether the end of the foreign military operation will be followed by increased Iraqi state authority over security and armed activities across the nation.

World.title: Trump hails end of US military presence in Iraq after 23 years
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – US President Donald Trump celebrated the departure of the final American soldiers from Iraq on Wednesday, describing it as a win for both nations and the end of a military chapter that started with the US-led invasion in 2003.

In a long social media statement announcing the pullout, Trump said that it was time for American soldiers to come home and criticized the initial decision to invade Iraq, portraying US participation in the nation as the product of bad decision-making and a costly struggle.

The White House also released Trump’s statements.

Trump praised the pullout as a success for both the United States and Iraq, as well as the end of the war against ISIS.

He also lauded Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Falih al-Zaidi, expressing faith in the Iraqi government’s capacity to assume responsibility for the country’s security.

The statements came after the United States Central Command concluded the evacuation of American soldiers and equipment from Erbil Air Base, thus ending Operation Inherent Resolve in Iraq.

The milestone comes 23 years after the US and its allies invaded Iraq in March 2003 and deposed Saddam Hussein, ushering in a volatile era marked by occupation, insurgency, sectarian violence, the development of ISIS, and the return of American soldiers in 2014.

The human cost to Iraq was immense.

Estimates vary based on methodology, but more than 200,000 Iraqi civilians have been murdered by direct violence since the 2003 invasion, with estimates of the overall death toll, including combatants and indirect fatalities connected with conflict, far higher.

The fighting displaced millions of Iraqis and severely damaged infrastructure and public services, with long-term implications.

US soldiers mostly departed from Iraq in 2011 but returned three years later at the request of the Iraqi government after ISIS took Mosul and vast portions of northern and western Iraq.

Throughout the battle against ISIS, the US-led coalition supplied air support, intelligence, training, and other aid to Iraqi troops and the Peshmerga.

Iraq claimed military victory over the organization in 2017, but ISIS cells continue to operate in areas of the nation.

Tom Barrack, US Ambassador to Turkey and Special Envoy to Iraq and Syria, also announced the pullout, portraying it as the end of a 23-year transition rather than Washington leaving Iraq.

In a post on X, Barrack said that the departure requires cooperation with Baghdad, Erbil, regional administrations, and Washington.

He said that it provided a chance for Iraq to consolidate its military forces under a single national authority, with the US becoming, in his words, “a friend rather than a garrison.”

That problem is likely to remain one of the most significant issues in Iraq’s post-coalition future.

Al-Zaidi’s administration has been working to restore state authority over weaponry owned by armed factions, including major Iran-aligned militias, while Baghdad takes main responsibility for national security.

The American withdrawal does not signal the end of security cooperation between Baghdad and Washington. The two nations are developing a bilateral defense partnership, while the US-led counter-ISIS campaign will continue elsewhere in the area.

For Iraq, however, September 30 marks the end of one of the longest and most significant eras in its modern history.

A whole generation of Iraqis has grown up with some form of US military involvement in the country, first after Saddam’s removal and then throughout the battle against ISIS.

The departure marks the beginning of a new chapter in which Iraq takes main responsibility for its own security, state authority, and destiny after more than two decades of conflict and foreign military occupation.

World.title: Swiss FA withdraws support for FIFA chief Infantino
World.content:
Geneva – The Swiss Football Association (SFV) announced Wednesday it was withdrawing its support for beleaguered incumbent Gianni Infantino in next year’s FIFA presidential election.

Several leading European national associations have pulled their support for Infantino, after he caused uproar in July with proposals to create a commercial subsidiary to run FIFA’s biggest events, such as the World Cup and Club World Cup.

The SFV’s decision carries weight as Infantino is Swiss, and both FIFA and European football’s governing body UEFA are based in Switzerland.

The SFV said its executive board met on Friday and “decided to withdraw the support it had declared in June 2026 for Gianni Infantino’s candidacy for a further term as FIFA president”.

Infantino’s plan would have allowed private investors to acquire stakes in a company created under the FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) initiative. The backlash that followed led to the proposals being quickly shelved.

The SFV said events in recent months raised fundamental questions over leadership, governance, transparency and decision-making processes with world football’s governing body.

It cited Infantino’s FFE plans and the lifting of red-carded United States forward Folarin Balogun’s one-match suspension during this year’s World Cup, following a phone call to Infantino from US President Donald Trump.

– ‘Special responsibility’ –

SFV president Peter Knabel said that Swiss football’s governing body expected FIFA’s leadership to uphold the highest standards of transparency, accountability and institutional responsibility.

He said Infantino’s proposals last week for “a consultation” with national federations to reform FIFA’s governance sent an important signal, and could contribute to improving the situation.

However, “key questions regarding the background, responsibilities and decision-making processes remain unanswered”, said Knabel.

“As these have not been convincingly clarified, we cannot justify continuing to support Gianni Infantino’s candidacy.”

UEFA — the regional federation that represents World Cup holders Spain and football powerhouses such as France, England and Germany — is leading the opposition to Infantino, calling openly for his removal.

The SFV, a UEFA member, insisted its decision did not signal a move away from constructive cooperation within FIFA and the global football community.

As the association for the country where FIFA and UEFA are based, “the SFV is aware of its special responsibility and will continue to champion transparency, credible and reliable structure, rules-based decision-making processes”, it said.

It called for a strong and united global football community characterised by integrity.

Infantino retains the support of 2034 World Cup hosts Saudi Arabia, while African football’s governing body CAF and South America’s CONMEBOL are also supportive.

Candidate nominations for next March’s FIFA election must be submitted by November 18. Infantino is the only candidate so far.

World.title: Oil companies close in on Venezuela despite hurdles
World.content:
Caracas – Foreign oil companies scrambled for a slice of Venezuela’s crude at an oil summit in Caracas this week despite years of sanctions, underinvestment and mismanagement that have crippled the once booming industry.

Venezuela sits on the world’s largest proven oil reserves, but its current production of one million barrels of crude per day falls far short of the three million it averaged decades ago, with experts attributing the decline to years of corruption and poor management.

The sold-out Venezuela International Oil and Gas Summit in Caracas, which runs until Wednesday, has attracted bosses from companies including European giants Repsol, Siemens, Maurel & Prom, US firm Hunt Oil Company, Qatari producer UCC Holding and Colombia’s GeoPark.

“Venezuela is the place to be,” Erik Keskula, director of exploration and production at UCC Oil and Gas Holding, said Tuesday.

US President Donald Trump, who wants to take charge of the country’s oil industry, has piled pressure on interim leader Delcy Rodriguez, who took power after the United States toppled president Nicolas Maduro in a military raid in January.

Rodriguez has granted Washington access to a huge chunk of the country’s crude reserves and signed agreements with foreign companies to look for, produce and export oil and gas.

North American Blue Energy Partners (NABEP), the company at the heart of a massive US-Venezuela deal in August to operate 17 oil fields with proven reserves of about 65 billion barrels, was not present at the summit.

According to a White House report, Washington holds veto power over NABEP’s board of directors, the majority of whom must be US citizens.

Critics in both the United States and Venezuela accuse Trump of holding the country to ransom after ousting Maduro and warning that Rodriguez could face a similar fate if she does not succumb to Washington’s demands.

Rodriguez insists Venezuela retains control of its oil.

– ‘Work to be done’ –

Organizers said hundreds of names were on a waiting list for the event, highlighting the industry buzz around Venezuela’s oil sector re-opening after years of state control.

Venezuela’s government, which remains under control of the ruling Chavista movement — named after late socialist firebrand Hugo Chavez — blames years of tough US sanctions for crippling the industry.

In 2019, during his first term in office, Trump imposed an embargo on Venezuelan oil in response to 2018 elections that were already marred by fraud allegations.

Venezuela’s state-owned PDVSA oil giant was in freefall at the time, beset by corruption scandals, mismanagement and a crippling lack of investment.

Oil output buckled under the weight of the sanctions.

“Real work remains on transparency, on governance, on ensuring that every dollar of revenue serves its intended purpose,” said Michael Garcia, deputy chief of mission at the US Embassy in Caracas.

“But the direction is unmistakable,” he said. “Where there was stagnation, there is now investment.”

Venezuela’s chronic electricity shortage was a key theme at the event, which was itself hit by two power cuts.

Hunter Hunt, CEO of Hunt Energy Holdings, said he was confident that such “infrastructural weaknesses” could be solved “quite quickly.”

– ‘Ambitious goal’ –

Companies already operating in Venezuela are pushing to boost production.

Ludwing Mercado, Repsol’s operations manager for Venezuela, said the company aimed to increase oil production by 50 percent in its oil fields in the country’s west.

When French firm Maurel & Prom secured a US license to operate in Venezuela this year — along with BP, Chevron, Eni, Repsol and Shell — bosses were “perhaps overly optimistic at the start,” deputy general manager Cesar Alvarez said.

“We drew up an action plan, but we ran up against reality and [had to] delay certain activities,” he said.

Despite the challenges, Maurel & Prom expects to close the year with an output of 23,000 barrels per day.

World.title: Iraq’s US dollar exchange rate slightly falls after days-long spike
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The exchange rate for the US dollar compared to the Iraqi dinar slightly declined on Wednesday in the Iraqi capital, Baghdad, and the capital of the Kurdistan region of Iraq, Erbil, following a days-long spike.

The US dollar exchange rate declined in Baghdad’s al-Kifah and al-Harithiya stock exchanges, reaching 1,570 Iraqi dinars compared to 1,572.5 Iraqi dinars on Wednesday morning.

The exchange rate in currency exchange shops in Baghdad ranged between 1,575 Iraqi dinars and 1,565 Iraqi dinars, Shafaq News reported.

In Erbil, the US dollar exchange rate also declined, fluctuating between 1,571.5 and 1,571 Iraqi dinars.

The Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) said in February 2023 that it has begun using the new US dollar exchange rate of 1,300 dinars for every US dollar.

The previous official exchange rate was 1,450 dinars to one US dollar, which was being exchanged in the parallel market at a rate of 1,550 dinars.

While the official exchange rate was 1,450 dinars per dollar in January 2023, the US currency was being exchanged at 1,610 dinars during the same month in the parallel market in Iraq. This variation indicated a difference of over 10 percent in the exchange rates.

World.title: Iraq declares conclusion of US-led mission, thanks member states
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister and Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces, Ali al-Zaidi, announced on Wednesday the conclusion of the US-led international coalition’s mission to combat ISIS in Iraq.

According to a statement released by the Iraqi government, al-Zaidi thanked the international coalition’s member states for their participation in defeating the terrorist group ISIS.

Al-Zaidi’s remarks took place during an official military event held in Baghdad to mark Iraq’s Sovereignty Day, a national holiday marking the withdrawal of US and international coalition forces from Iraq.

The event marked the formal conclusion of the Combined Joint Task Force – Operation Inherent Resolve, following the complete withdrawal of coalition forces and equipment from key military bases in Iraq.

Al-Zaidi thanked the international coalition’s member states, commanders, and advisers, stating that collaboration has effectively overcome a difficult period of extremism.

The handover is an indication of Iraq’s full responsibility for the security and stability of the country, as well as combating terrorism.

Addressing armed factions, al-Zaidi declared that there shall be no firearms outside the framework of the law and no force outside the institutions of the state.

The Iraqi prime minister said earlier that October 1, 2026, will mark a new day in Iraq’s statehood when the country achieves complete sovereignty free of foreign troops.

Iraq’s future engagements with the international coalition’s member nations will center on direct security, economic, and specialized training cooperation based on mutual respect.

The international coalition was first formed in 2014 to combat the emergence of the terrorist group ISIS.

After Iraq declared the defeat of ISIS in 2017, international coalition forces continued to offer assistance and training services at Baghdad’s request.

World.title: US reports firm Q2 economic growth, inflation steady
World.content:
Washington – The United States on Wednesday estimated stronger second-quarter GDP growth than previously reported, with inflation remaining steady and private payrolls increasing more than expected.

The US Commerce Department revised upwards its estimate for Q2 GDP growth in the world’s largest economy by 0.7 percentage points to 2.2 percent.

“The contributors to the increase in real GDP in the second quarter were consumer spending, investment, and exports. Imports, which are a subtraction in the calculation of GDP, increased,” the Bureau of Economic Analysis said in a statement.

The new data will come as a boost to US President Donald Trump as his Republican Party heads into key midterm elections in November, with the state of the economy a major issue for voters.

In terms of specific industries, the leading contributors to the increase were real estate, information, durable goods manufacturing, and finance and insurance, the BEA said.

Decreases came from the transportation and retail trade, as well as from non-durable goods manufacturing.

The BEA also revised upwards its estimate of GDP growth in the first quarter of this year by 0.4 percentage points to 2.5 percent.

That change was primarily driven by upward revisions to consumer spending and services exports, the department said.

– Inflation steady –

In a separate release, the BEA said the US Federal Reserve’s preferred inflation gauge stood at 3.4 percent year-on-year in August, unchanged from the month before after a revision to the July data.

US households and businesses have been battered by years of high prices since the pandemic, with the Fed missing its long-term two-percent target for inflation since early 2021.

Earlier this month, the Fed raised interest rates for the first time in three years to combat the inflation.

The Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price index, the Fed’s targeted gauge, covers a broader range of household spending than the other benchmark metric, the Consumer Price Index (CPI).

US inflation has been stoked by some of Trump’s policies, including his imposition of widespread tariffs. His launching of the Iran war has sent global energy prices skyrocketing, with US consumers paying an average of 50 percent more at the pump.

Core PCE inflation, which strips out volatile energy and food prices, came in at 3.0 percent year-over-year.

Markets are closely watching inflation data to gauge the Fed’s next move.

On Tuesday, an influential US central banker said there was no “urgency” to raise rates again, even as he indicated one more rate hike could be needed before the end of the year.

– Private payrolls bounce back –

The US labor market has been largely stable this year, allowing the Fed to concentrate on the inflation side of its dual mandate.

On Wednesday, payroll firm ADP reported that US private sector hiring had bounced back strongly in September, after registering its slowest pace this year the month before.

Private sector job growth came in at 90,000 last month, up from 38,000 the month before and well above market expectations.

“It’s a strong report,” said Nela Richardson, ADP’s chief economist. “After a three-month slowdown, job creation rebounded and pay growth remained solid.”

ADP’s data is closely monitored ahead of official employment numbers due Friday, although the reports can diverge.

Matthew Martin, senior US economist at Oxford Economics, said ADP’s data underscored “the strength of the labor market.”

It “will bolster market expectations for firmer monetary policy from the Federal Reserve as it seeks to ensure inflation is tamped out,” he added.

World.title: Bengal government stalling MP work: Mahua
World.content:
NEW DELHI: TMC MP

Wednesday complained to SC that

government in West Bengal has made it impossible for her to function as a member of Parliament by stalling her MPLAD fund related works, impeding her visits to her constituency Krishnanagar and allowing goons to harass her.

Though her counsel Gopal Sankaranarayanan could not be present to argue her case due to preoccupation in other court, solicitor general Tushar Mehta questioned whether an MP could move SC directly bypassing Calcutta HC, which is best suited to examine the allegations relating to incidents that took place in its jurisdiction. Moitra said developmental work worth Rs 3.5 crore initiated through her MPLAD funds have been stalled as officials have stopped cooperating with her.

World.title: Must pass on benefits of growth to next generation: Rijiju
World.content:
NEW DELHI: India is the fastest growing major economy in the world and the challenge is to extend that growth and pass on its benefits to the next generation, said Union minister of parliamentary affairs and minority affairs

.

Speaking at the Times Now Amazing Indians Awards 2026 he highlighted the importance of freedom of expression. He added, "We are fortunate to be part of this great society... If there are people who are not feeling part of the growth story, then it is our duty as a part of govt to bring them along... people must have different opinions, or different beliefs..."

Tukaram Mundhe, Commissioner, Food and Drug Administration, Maharashtra, received the Special Recognition for Public Service.

The initiative honoured changemakers across diverse fields, recognising individuals who are driving meaningful impact in society. Colonel Dr Navaz Shariff and Parveen Shaikh were named joint winners in Animal Welfare & Wildlife Conservation, while Anita Agarwal and Sayera Rahman shared the honour in Disability - Care, Rehabilitation & Developmental Support. World.title: To Bengal plea on Congress pick, SC says will dismiss appeal
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Applying its recently framed policy of rejecting challenges to bails granted by high courts, Supreme Court on Wednesday told the West Bengal govt that it would dismiss the state's appeal against grant of interim bail to Milan Pradhan, Congress candidate for the Nandigram assembly bypoll, who is an accused in a 2007 murder case.

A CJI-led bench expressed difficulty to list the matter on Thursday and said, "Instead of Thursday, we will dismiss the appeal on Monday."

By Monday, electioneering for the bypoll would be over and the state's appeal would be infructuous. Solicitor general Tushar Mehta, appearing for the state, requested a bench headed by CJI Surya Kant for a hearing on Thursday of the appeal challenging the grant of interim bail to Pradhan for canvassing for the election scheduled for Oct 6, campaigning for which will end on Oct 4.

When the bench said since the HC had granted only interim bail, it would not entertain such an appeal, Mehta brought up Pradhan's history sheet -- accused in a murder case and featuring in six other FIRs on serious crimes -- to request a hearing on Thursday.

The HC had, citing the relief the SC gave to AAP leader Arvind Kejriwal, granted bail to Pradhan on Tuesday and asked him to surrender before the additional chief judicial magistrate, Haldia, on Oct 21.





Counting of votes in Nandigram, which was vacated by chief minister Suvendu Adhikari who also won from Bhabanipur, will happen on Oct 9.

The state said in its appeal, "The HC granted interim bail to Pradhan, an accused charged with multiple counts of heinous offences including murder, arson, bomb blasts and rioting with deadly weapons, solely on the untenable pretext of permitting him to participate in an election."

World.title: Supreme Court allows sale, manufacture of next-generation green firecrackers
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Ahead of the festive season, Supreme Court on Wednesday paved the way for the manufacture and sale of next-generation joined green firecrackers after Centre's recommendation.

Commonly known as 'ladi', these were earlier banned by the court.

SC also said a separate order would be passed for Delhi and indicated that while the bursting of firecrackers would not be banned, the activity would not be allowed at all hours.

Additional solicitor general Aishwarya Bhati told a bench of justices M M Sundresh and Prasanna B Varale that government had recommended that joined firecrackers, which complied with norms fixed by Council of Scientific and Industrial Research-National Environmental Engineering Research Institute (CSIR-NEERI), be allowed.

The issue of using barium chemical remains undecided as the ASG told the bench that field trials were on, and sought time till Oct 15.

Submitting the findings of CSIR-NEERI, Bhati said the report said 25 braids were burst in one second in conventional joined firecrackers whereas in next-generation joined firecrackers, only five braids were burst in a second.

Government said manufacturers must comply with specifications/formulations tested and approved by the competent authority as well as with the prescribed noise limit and emission and safety requirements fixed under the law.





Advocate Pranav Sachdeva, appearing for some manufacturers, assured the bench they would do so.

As the pollution crisis in winter has become an annual affair in Delhi, the bench said it would pass a separate order for the national capital. "We're making this very clear. Neither are we going to agree with you for a total ban nor are we going to allow it 24 hours," the court said.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

A total ban would have a "sentimental effect", SC said, but allowing bursting of crackers throughout the day would have a "huge impact on every other living being, including old people, sick people and children".

"We need to find a solution whereby we can give specified time and we can specify what crackers are to be used," the bench told the petitioner seeking curbs on the sale of firecrackers in NCR.

Earlier, two government organisations had taken contradictory stands in SC on allowing next-generation green firecrackers. While CSIR-NEERI approved them saying their pollution levels had decreased by 40-60% and recommended commercial production of flowerpots, sparklers, 'chakkars', pencils, 'ladis' and twinkling stars, Central Pollution Control Board said they contained barium nitrate, which was banned by SC.

World.title: Second full EC meet in 5 days, SIR extended again in Andhra Pradesh, Meghalaya
World.content:
Chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar with election commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi

NEW DELHI: The full Election Commission - comprising CEC Gyanesh Kumar and ECs S S Sandhu and Vivek Joshi - met Wednesday, a second time in five days, and decided to extend the deadlines for the ongoing SIR exercise in Andhra Pradesh and Meghalaya, reports Bharti Jain.The revised period for disposal of claims and objections in Andhra will now run from July 31 to Oct 10. The date for publication of the final poll roll also stands extended to Oct 16. For Meghalaya, the date for publication of the final poll roll has been revised to Oct 26.The second full meeting of the commission since an Indian Express report alleged that ECs Sandhu and Joshi had objected to steps taken by EC on 14 occasions over 10 months reaffirms that the CEC and the two ECs have agreed to sit together and transact normal business of the commission through regular meetings.The draft roll of Meghalaya published on Aug 5 listed 21.7 lakh electors, with around 7.7% absent, shifted, dead and duplicate electors deleted. In Andhra, the draft roll listed 3.7 crore electors after deleting 10.8% of its electorate.

World.title: Trump says flydubai pilot 'a hero', plumber steadied plunging aircraft
World.content:
U.S. President Donald Trump hailed the flydubai pilot as a "hero" for fighting off a knife attack from the co-pilot, opening the cockpit door and calling for help to foil a bid to crash the aircraft.

Interacting with reporters at the Oval Office, Mr. Trump said he spoke to Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who told him that a plumber, who had never flown an aircraft, made a dramatic intervention to steady the Dubai-Tel Aviv flight which landed in Saudi Arabia.

The pilot who staved off the attempt to crash the aircraft has been identified as Smit Machchhar, an Indian national, and hailed a "hero" by Mr. Netanyahu and many others.

"The pilot was in very bad shape; I guess he still is in very bad shape, but he had the sense to, amazing, to, in a way he was a hero," Mr. Trump said, recalling his conversation with Netanyahu.

Mr. Trump said the pilot opened the door and was able to fall back, get the door open and scream for help.

"It seems as though the co-pilot was perhaps a terrorist or perhaps a whack job, and he stabbed the pilot," the U.S. President said.

Mr. Trump then described what he called an "amazing" intervention by an Israeli passenger whom he identified as a plumber.

Mr. Trump said a passenger, who had never flown an aircraft, entered the cockpit, pulled the co-pilot out of his seat and threw him backwards, where other passengers helped restrain him.

According to Mr. Trump, the passenger later said he had learned some basic concepts about flying from watching the television program Air Disasters.

"He said he watches it a lot, and he learned from watching that show sort of how to fly," Mr. Trump said.

Mr. Trump said additional pilots and security personnel, who had been toward the rear of the aircraft, subsequently reached the cockpit and took control.

"I think it’s the most amazing story," he said.

However, Mr. Trump said that he was merely recounting an account he had received rather than independently confirmed facts.

"Now this is the story that I heard. I don’t know if it’s true, but that’s the story that I got from Bibi and from a couple of probably early [sources]," he said.

World.title: Kalamassery police issue fresh summons to Anto Augustine in case over ‘CM marriage remarks’
World.content:
The Kalamassery police have issued fresh summons to Reporter TV managing director Anto Augustine and two unidentified people over the alleged defamatory remarks that he made against Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan.

Mr. Augustine has been asked to appear before investigators at 10 a.m. on Thursday (October 1, 2026), a senior police officer said. The fresh summons was issued after Mr. Augustine did not turn up at the station on Monday for interrogation citing inconvenience. He has also moved the High Court seeking to quash the first information report in the case.

The case pertains to an alleged revelation made by Mr. Augustine that two people had met him with what they claimed was a journalistic scoop on Mr. Satheesan’s alleged second marriage. He claimed that his channel did not telecast the news after his team could not verify the allegation. The case was registered on a complaint filed by Congress spokesperson Raju P. Nair, alleging conspiracy behind the revelation.

World.title: Kerala High Court directs State govt. to expedite disposal of pending cases against MPs and MLAs based on District Judiciary recommendations
World.content:
The Kerala High Court has directed the Keralam government to expedite the disposal of pending cases against MPs and MLAs in accordance with the recommendations of the District Judiciary Registrar.

The court was considering a suo motu petition initiated under Supreme Court directives to monitor pending cases against sitting/former MPs and MLAs.

The Registrar suggested measures such as prioritising the execution of processes such as summons or warrants issued by criminal courts and deputing police officers to assist courts in the matter. The Registrar said that two police officers from each station shall be deputed exclusively for process duty, and that their duty diaries should be monitored accordingly. The functioning of nodal officers should be strengthened through frequent meetings.

It was also recommended to implement the Kerala Electronic Processes (Issuance, Service and Execution) Rules, 2025, where a person could be notified of proceedings through WhatsApp. The recipient could verify the authenticity of such a notification by using the verification facility on the District Case Management Services (DCMS) portal.

Additionally, the reconstitution of committees for coordination among different criminal justice functionaries at the magistrate, district and State level was recommended.

Wherever possible, videoconferencing facilities were suggested to ensure the appearance of accused persons and witnesses to avoid unnecessary delay in proceedings.

Referring to the police station-wise process register available online in DCMS, the Registrar recommended developing a corresponding facility at stations to record details of the case and the action taken in the proceedings. Further, processes that remained unexecuted beyond the prescribed period could be separately flagged for immediate follow-up.

World.title: Hyderabad landmarks turn pink to observe breast cancer awareness month
World.content:
Eight landmarks in Hyderabad turned pink on Wednesday evening as the Ushalakshmi Breast Cancer Foundation (UBF) launched its 18th annual ‘Paint the City Pink’ campaign to mark the beginning of International Breast Cancer Awareness Month.

The campaign, launched in 2009, has been held for 18 consecutive years, even during the COVID-19 pandemic.

“Hyderabad is the only city in the world where several iconic monuments and prominent buildings have been illuminated in pink on the same night for 18 consecutive years,” said UBF founding director P. Raghu Ram.

World.title: Centre’s final nod for Vizag Metro Rail project awaited
World.content:
The long-anticipated Visakhapatnam Metro Rail project has inched closer to realisation as the State infrastructure authorities await the final statutory and financial clearances from New Delhi.

The mass rapid transit system, envisioned to ease traffic congestion and modernise urban mobility across the port city, is currently moving through critical administrative reviews at the national level.

Speaking to The Hindu on September 30, Andhra Pradesh Metro Rail Corporation (APMRC) Managing Director N.P. Ramakrishna Reddy stated, “It is under process at the Centre level.” The comprehensive project layout outlines extensive multi-tier corridors designed to connect key industrial nodes, commercial districts, and residential neighborhoods.

State transport planners have updated the Detailed Project Report to align with national urban transit standards and ongoing highway expansions, aiming to minimise private land acquisition while maximising public utility.

A significant portion of the land required for the initial corridors comprises government-owned parcels, which is expected to streamline execution once final approvals are unlocked. The cooperative financial framework relies on a shared model involving both central and State equity, alongside external developmental assistance.

Transport department officials are maintaining active coordination with central ministries to expedite the clearance of files.

Once the official green light is issued by the Union government, the State administration is slated to fast-track subsequent milestones, including formal land integration, final route demarcations, and the rollout of global tenders for civil construction and specialised electrical traction networks.

Residents and commuters across the city continue to monitor developments closely, anticipating an upgrade to regional public transportation infrastructure that will support future economic expansion. The revised Phase-I blueprint of the metro project spans an estimated total cost of ₹11,498 crore. Structured to cover 46.23 kilometres across core corridors featuring 43 modern stations, the network will strategically link high-density residential hubs, commercial zones, and industrial layouts.

The initial phase blueprints focus heavily on optimising public transit efficiency while synchronizing alignments with upcoming national highway expansions to minimise private land acquisition. External development financing, including funding support discussions with multilateral institutions like the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB) to back roughly 60% of the project, alongside joint equity contributions from the central and State governments.

World.title: Asian Games 2026: Andhra athletes win three golds, a bronze
World.content:
Athletes from Andhra Pradesh have bagged three gold medals and a bronze at the Asian Games in Japan so far, with archery, cricket and badminton all contributing to the tally.

Nine athletes from the State are competing, according to Ramana, Section Officer (Associations), Sports Authority of Andhra Pradesh. They are badminton players P.V. Sindhu, Satwiksairaj Rankireddy, Kidambi Srikanth and Kavipriya Selvam; cricketer Sree Charani; archers Dhiraj Bommadevara, Thirumuru Ganesh Mani Ratnam and Jyothi Surekha Vennam; and hurdler Jyothi Yarraji.

On Wednesday, (September 30, 2026) Jyothi Surekha and Ganesh clinched gold as India swept all three compound archery team titles at Okazaki City. Jyothi Surekha, with Chikitha Taniparthi and Prithika Pradeep, beat China 238-234, equalling the world record. Ganesh, from Naidupeta in Tirupati district, joined Kushal Dalal and Sahil Jadhav to edge China 238-237 after overcoming South Korea in the semi-final.

President Droupadi Murmu told the women’s team that their “precision, composure and teamwork have made the nation proud”. Of the men’s win, she said, “Completing a clean sweep of Gold across all three Compound Team events, Indian archery has achieved a remarkable feat.”

Heartiest congratulations to Sahil Rajesh Jadhav, Ganesh Maniratnam Thirumuru and Kushal Dalal on winning the Gold Medal in the Compound Men's Team event at the Asian Games 2026!



Completing a clean sweep of Gold across all three Compound Team events, Indian archery has achieved… — President of India (@rashtrapatibhvn) September 30, 2026

Prime Minister Narendra Modi said the women’s win “is even more special because their performance also equalled the World Record”. Union Sports Minister Mansukh Mandaviya called the men’s gold “a proud moment for Indian archery and for the entire nation”.

Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu said Ganesh’s “path from Naidupeta to international glory stands as a testament to what focus and hard work can accomplish”. Deputy Chief Minister K. Pawan Kalyan said the women’s team had “brought the Tricolour to the highest podium”. IT Minister Nara Lokesh called Ganesh’s journey “a matter of immense pride for our State”.

A moment of immense pride for #AndhraPradesh and the entire nation!



My heartiest congratulations to Ganesh Mani Ratnam Thirumuru, along with Sahil Jadhav and Kushal Dalal, on winning the Gold Medal in Men's Compound Archery at the #AsianGames2026!



Holding their composure in… pic.twitter.com/gpSvM4PrTN — N Chandrababu Naidu (@ncbn) September 30, 2026

The men’s badminton team won bronze. Every member of the squad, including Satwiksairaj and Srikanth, receives a medal, Mr. Ramana said. India lost 3-1 to China in the semi-final at Ichinomiya.

For Jyothi Surekha, Wednesday’s gold is her sixth medal across four consecutive Asian Games: four gold, one silver and one bronze. “Her experience is a major advantage,” said her father, Surendra Kumar, speaking from Vijayawada.

Sport runs in the family, he said. She began swimming as a child and, at five, swam across the Krishna, a feat recorded in the Limca Book of Records. She took up archery at 12. “Because we have seen her go through that experience from childhood, her achievements do not seem entirely unexpected to us,” Mr. Surendra Kumar said.

The Volga Archery Academy in Vijayawada, run by Cherukuri Satyanarayana, has produced several of the State’s leading archers. Mr. Satyanarayana, Vice-President of the Archery Association of India and chairman of the A.P. Archery Association, attributed the archers’ success to discipline, concentration and timing.

Among its trainees is Dhiraj, who set an Asian Games record of 698 in the recurve ranking round and has reached the individual quarter-finals and the team semi-final.
